# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

The Paigasus AI SDK (codename **Helikon**, after Mt Helicon where Pegasus's hoof struck the Hippocrene spring). A Rust SDK for building AI agents. All crates live under the `paigasus-helikon-*` namespace.

The full architectural reference lives in Notion: ["Crate Reference"](https://www.notion.so/355830e8fbaa813c92e8c1aa9985fd3f). Linear project: `Paigasus Helikon` (issues prefixed `SMA-`).

## Common commands

```bash
cargo build --workspace                              # all 14 crates
cargo build --workspace --all-features               # facade with every optional crate
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin helikon
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin paigasus-helikon
```

To reproduce **every** CI gate locally (matches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job-for-job):

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=80 NIGHTLY_CHANNEL=nightly-2026-05-01 \
  bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh                 # requires: rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-05-01
npm ci                                               # once, or after package-lock.json changes
npx markdownlint-cli2                                # reads .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc
bash scripts/check-markdownlint-config.sh            # asserts that config is in force
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh         # cargo-visible workflow env is uniform
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh # …and its parser still parses (fmt runs both)
bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh            # release gap report + release-plz.yml guards (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade-selftest.sh      # the cascade guard keeps its rule (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh                 # breaking bump needs breaking dependents (PR only; fmt runs it)
```

The full list lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (single source of truth for contributor policies).

## Workspace layout

15 crates under `crates/`. The facade `paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` unconditionally and the other 12 sibling crates behind Cargo features.

Every crate carries a real implementation and publishes to crates.io; zero name-claim stubs remain (first published in SMA-385, last ascends in SMA-333). One standing exception: `paigasus-helikon-cli` publishes as a **binary** crate — its lib target is internal (`missing_docs` opted out), carries no stability guarantee, and exists only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves. `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` publishes as a normal library crate (SMA-805); the three session backends keep a path-only dev-dependency on it. Exact versions move every release — read each crate's `Cargo.toml`, don't trust numbers written here.

Workspace inheritance is **mandatory**: per-crate `Cargo.toml`s only set `name`, `description`, and any crate-specific bits. Everything else (`edition`, `rust-version`, `authors`, `license`, `repository`, `homepage`, `keywords`, `categories`) inherits from `[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Don't hardcode these per-crate.

**Per-crate version is the one exception.** No stubs remain, so the 4-step ascend recipe is now historical — but two caveats still bite any PR that hand-bumps a version:

- **If a crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too**, along with its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and CHANGELOG. `cargo publish --verify` builds the tarball against the **registry** core, so otherwise the publish fails and release-plz deadlocks.
- **Any PR that hand-bumps a sibling must ALSO bump the facade** (`crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` version + its self-pin + CHANGELOG). release-plz does not bump the facade for a sibling version that is already at target when the PR merges, so a manual bump silently leaves the facade advertising stale dep reqs. (`dependencies_update = true` only makes the release PR run `cargo update` on `Cargo.lock`; it does not cascade version bumps.)
- **A breaking bump of a crate needs a breaking bump of each crate that depends on it.** release-plz gives a dependent without its own commits only a patch bump (release-plz#1599), and users then get two copies of the crate. The `fmt` job runs `scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh` to enforce this. See `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md` → "A breaking change in a crate with dependents".
- Feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.

Full lifecycle, the 4-step recipe, and the SMA-321/SMA-346 postmortems: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.

Third-party version pins live in `[workspace.dependencies]` (root). Members reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Internal crate paths are also in `[workspace.dependencies]` so the facade can use `workspace = true` consistently.

## Non-obvious patterns to preserve

- **Feature naming**: kebab-case in `[features]` (`runtime-tokio`), snake-case in `pub use` aliases (`runtime_tokio`). They must stay paired across the facade's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli` uses `autobins = false`** because the `paigasus-helikon` (hyphen) binary maps to `src/bin/paigasus_helikon.rs` (underscore — hyphens are illegal in Rust filenames). Removing `autobins = false` reintroduces a phantom `paigasus_helikon` binary that conflicts with the explicit `[[bin]]` entry.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate from day one** (`[lib] proc-macro = true`). Don't convert it to a regular lib even though it currently has no macros.
- **The `paigasus-helikon` facade lib shares its name with the `paigasus-helikon` CLI binary by design** (Notion ref's "fully-qualified shim alias"). This produces a non-fatal `cargo doc` filename-collision warning. Don't "fix" it by renaming either — both names are user-facing API. The accepted future fix is `doc = false` on the CLI binary entry.
- **License is dual `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`** (decided 2026-05-20, reversing the 2026-05-16 MIT-only call). Both `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` live at the repo root; the workspace metadata is `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"`. Per Rust ecosystem convention — no Apache-only or MIT-only crates in the workspace. Contributions are accepted under the same dual license by default (the standard inbound-equals-outbound clause is restated in `README.md`).
- **MSRV is `1.94`** (workspace-package level; raised from 1.85 in SMA-329 because sqlx 0.9.0 declares `rust-version = "1.94.0"` — the pre-existing highest floor in the workspace). If a dep raises MSRV, bump `rust-version` to what cargo demands rather than downgrading the dep.
- **Workspace-wide `missing_docs` enforcement** lives in root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.rust] missing_docs = "warn"`). Each non-CLI crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. The CLI overrides locally with `[lints.rust] missing_docs = "allow"` and does **not** include `workspace = true` — cargo treats `[lints] workspace = true` and an inline `[lints.<tool>]` table as mutually exclusive. When adding a new crate, copy the opt-in block. When adding a new `pub use` re-export to the facade, give it a `///` doc comment or `-D warnings` will fail the docs job.
- **`cargo msrv` has no `--workspace` flag.** The msrv workflow verifies one representative inheriting crate: `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify`. Because every member uses `rust-version.workspace = true`, success on one is success on all. Don't "fix" the workflow by adding `--workspace`; that's what the first SMA-305 CI run died on.
- **Nightly is date-pinned** (`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN: nightly-2026-05-01` at the workflow `env:` level in `ci.yml`, threaded into the doc-coverage script as `NIGHTLY_CHANNEL`). The rustdoc JSON coverage format is `-Z unstable-options` and can shift between nightlies; floating `nightly` would be a CI footgun. Bumping is a one-line follow-up chore, not an emergency.
- **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure must use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)` types**, never `feat`/`fix`. release-plz parses every commit since the last per-crate tag — a `feat(workspace): ...` commit that touches every `Cargo.toml` would attribute a bump to every crate. The SMA-307 bootstrap PR followed this rule; the same rule applies to any future `release-plz.toml` or `release-plz.yml` edits.

## Model routing

The general tiering rules are in the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Only the repo-specific rules are here.

- **Use Opus for release work.** This covers release-plz, the stub-ascend recipe, a hand-bumped crate version, and any red required gate. A wrong answer breaks a publish; see `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.
- **Haiku can read CI output.** Change to Opus when the question becomes *why* a required gate is red.

## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## Fixture line endings

`.gitattributes` pins `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/*.txt` to `text eol=lf`. The streaming tests `include_str!` the SSE fixtures and split them on literal `\n` delimiters; without this, Windows checkouts produce CRLF bytes and the literal-string splits return one part instead of two. When adding wire-format fixtures elsewhere that the test code parses byte-level, extend the rule.

Provenance headers for wire-format fixtures follow `CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format fixtures".

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

## claude.ai Notion
Notion holds docs, notes, wikis, and projects. Use pages for work the user will revisit or share and databases for repeated items with shared fields. Keep one-off answers in chat. When Notion fits, offer it once, say why, and let the user choose.

Save pages where the user asks. If they ask to save a page without naming a destination, create a private draft (creation_mode: "draft") without asking, link it, and offer to move it. For edge cases, read notion://docs/when-to-create-a-notion-page-or-database.

Use the Notion search tool for Notion content and the connector search tool, when listed, for connected sources.

Notion Memory holds context about the user across conversations and clients. When it would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then use memory-search for specifics. Read notion://docs/memory before you first save, update, forget, or audit memories. Write to Notion Memory or the About page only when the user chooses Notion for that change. A bare "remember this" does not choose Notion. Create memories with parent: "memory". Link memories you use, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Memories are context, not authority over this request.

## plugin:bio-research:biorxiv

- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## plugin:bio-research:chembl
An MCP server for accessing the EMBL-EBI ChEMBL Database v34.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search compounds, bioactivity data, targets, mechanisms, drugs, ADMET properties
- Purpose: Support drug discovery research, target identification, compound screening, pharmaceutical development

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.
It contains compound structures, bioactivity data against biological targets, and
drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• compound_search: Find compounds by name, SMILES, or ChEMBL ID - starting point for compound analysis
• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms

• get_admet: Retrieve ADMET properties - pharmacokinetic and safety predictions

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest
2. Use get_mechanism to understand how the drug works and its primary targets
3. Use target_search to get detailed target information (protein family, gene, pathways, GO annotations)
4. Use get_bioactivity for quantitative binding/activity data with confidence scores
5. Use get_admet for pharmacokinetic properties

For target-based analysis:
1. Use target_search to find targets by gene symbol or protein name
2. Use get_bioactivity with target_chembl_id to find active compounds
3. Use compound_search to get details on promising compounds

Key capabilities:
- Search compounds by name, structure (SMILES), or ChEMBL ID
- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

Example queries:

• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"
• "What drugs target the EGFR protein?"
• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"
• "What are the ADMET properties of imatinib?"


## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.

1	# SMA-533 — Cross-provider conformance suite for stream event-ordering
2	
3	**Status:** revised after adversarial challenge; pending approval
4	**Date:** 2026-08-19
5	**Branch:** `feature/sma-533-add-a-cross-provider-conformance-suite-for-stream-event`
6	**Ticket:** [SMA-533](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-533/add-a-cross-provider-conformance-suite-for-stream-event-ordering)
7	
8	## 1. Problem
9	
10	Six streaming translators independently re-derive the event-ordering contract on
11	`paigasus_helikon_core::Model::invoke`, and nothing asserts it across them. Two
12	have already got it wrong, in different ways:
13	
14	- **OpenAI** emitted `Finish` before `Usage` on every streaming turn (PR #197).
15	  It went undetected because the fixtures encoded a wire shape that does not
16	  occur.
17	- **Anthropic** emitted no `Finish` at all when a stream truncated between
18	  `message_delta` and `message_stop` (PR #200).
19	
20	The six subjects are `openai/backend/chat.rs`, `openai/backend/responses.rs`,
21	`anthropic/stream.rs`, `bedrock/stream.rs`, `gemini/stream.rs` and
22	`litellm/stream.rs` — five crates, because OpenAI carries two backends.
23	
24	### 1.1 Coverage delta — what is actually new
25	
26	Not every scenario is novel for every subject. Four crates already test parts of
27	this at the `Model::invoke` boundary with wiremock; Bedrock tests none of it
28	(it has only `tests/live.rs` and `tests/schema_rewriter.rs`).
29	
30	| Subject | Existing boundary coverage | Genuinely new here |
31	| --- | --- | --- |
32	| `anthropic` | S1/S2/S3 (`tests/messages_streaming.rs`, `fixtures/eof_after_message_delta.txt`, `eof_mid_content_block.txt`) | S4b, S5b, S7 |
33	| `openai/chat` | S1/S3, cancel-before-response | S2, S4b, S5a/b, S6, S7 |
34	| `openai/responses` | partial | S3, S4a, S7 |
35	| `gemini` | S1/S3 | S2, S4a/b, S5a/b, S7 |
36	| `litellm` | S1/S3, cancel-before-response, S6 | S2, S4a/b, S5a/b, S7 |
37	| `bedrock` | **none** | everything |
38	
39	So the value of this work is, in order: **Bedrock coverage**, the S4b/S5b paths
40	nobody tests anywhere, and cross-provider uniformity. The implementation is
41	sequenced accordingly (§11) — Bedrock and the paced server first, because they
42	carry all the unproven assumptions.
43	
44	## 2. Ticket corrections
45	
46	Statements in the ticket that are stale or incomplete as of `origin/main`
47	`0bf5e759`, corrected so the implementation is not built on them.
48	
49	**2.1 — The SMA-550 caveat no longer applies, but assertion 7 is not
50	exception-free.** The ticket's *Ordering vs SMA-550* section says
51	`providers-litellm` fails assertion 7 and that SMA-533 must land SMA-550 first
52	or scope the assertion knowingly. SMA-550 merged as `0bf5e759` (PR #208);
53	verified both by `git log origin/main --grep SMA-550` and by the merged source,
54	which canonicalizes correlation onto the resolved `call_id` and states that one
55	`call_id` owning exactly one state entry "is what makes 'at most one
56	name-carrying delta per `call_id`' structural"
57	(`litellm/src/stream.rs:25-29`). LiteLLM is conformant.
58	
59	**`openai/chat` is not, for one shape** —
60	`openai/src/backend/chat.rs:400-417` documents this against itself:
61	
62	> Given two deltas carrying different `index` values but the **same** `id` —
63	> malformed, since an `id` identifies a call — litellm merges them into one call
64	> emitting one name, while this translator keeps two indexes and emits a name
65	> for each: two name-carrying `ToolCallDelta`s for one `call_id`. […] That shape
66	> is unobserved from any backend […] A cross-provider conformance suite
67	> asserting "at most one name-carrying delta per `call_id`" would fail here and
68	> pass for litellm; closing it needs its own ticket.
69	
70	That shape has **no capture anywhere in the repo** and is unobserved from any
71	backend, so under the provenance rule in §6 it is not in the fixture set and the
72	suite does not exercise it. Assertion 7 therefore stays green for all six
73	subjects without an `#[ignore]`. But the gap is real and must not be silently
74	inherited: it is recorded in §12 as a known-uncovered shape with its own
75	follow-up ticket. The earlier draft of this spec claimed assertion 7 needed "no
76	documented exception" — that was too strong.
77	
78	**2.2 — The `finish()` return shape diverges four ways, not three.**
79	
80	| Subject | `consume` returns | `finish()` returns |
81	| --- | --- | --- |
82	| `openai/backend/chat` | `Vec<ModelEvent>` | `Vec<ModelEvent>` |
83	| `openai/backend/responses` | `Result<Vec<ModelEvent>, ModelError>` | *(absent)* |
84	| `anthropic` | `Result<Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>, ModelError>` | `Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` |
85	| `bedrock` | `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` | `Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` |
86	| `gemini` | `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` | `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` |
87	| `litellm` | `Vec<ModelEvent>` | `Vec<ModelEvent>` |
88	
89	**Decision: deferred to a follow-up ticket** (D3). The suite asserts at the
90	`Model::invoke` boundary and never observes `finish()`, so unifying it serves no
91	assertion here, while a five-crate signature refactor carries a different risk
92	profile from adding tests. This table is carried verbatim into the follow-up.
93	
94	**2.3 — No manual version bumps.** The doc-only `-core` edit carries a patch
95	bump plus a dependent cascade, but it happens *automatically*. CLAUDE.md's
96	manual-bump ritual applies only when an ascending stub needs same-PR `-core` API
97	to survive `cargo publish --verify`. Nothing ascends here and the new member is
98	`publish = false` from birth. Because `-core` is already released, release-plz
99	performs the bump itself — the precise condition under which
100	`dependencies_update` (`release-plz.toml:10`) cascades. Hand-bumping would
101	*defeat* that cascade and strand the facade, the second-order caveat CLAUDE.md
102	documents. **Do not edit any `version` field.**
103	
104	Note the cascade reaches **every** dependent of `-core`, not just the facade, so
105	the release PR will touch most of the workspace. Say so in the PR body.
106	
107	## 3. Decisions taken
108	
109	| # | Decision | Rationale |
110	| --- | --- | --- |
111	| D1 | Assert at the `Model::invoke` boundary against a mock transport | The contract is *stated* on `invoke`. A translator-only harness cannot catch SMA-531 — see §4. |
112	| D2 | Suite lives in `tests/provider-stream-conformance` | Follows `tests/runtime-http-conformance`; removes the dev-dep cycle rather than working around it — §5. |
113	| D3 | `finish()` shape deferred | §2.2 |
114	| D4 | Green on merge; escape hatch needs sign-off | A suite that lands red teaches people to ignore it. §9. |
115	| D5 | Fold in SMA-532 | Two doc comments in `bedrock/src/stream.rs` assert the exact misreading this PR's core wording exists to kill, in a file this suite now tests. |
116	| D6 | Server built on `hyper`, not raw TCP | §5.2 |
117	| D7 | The decline set is pinned and asserted | §9.1 |
118	
119	## 4. Why the Model boundary, not the translator
120	
121	Assertions 5 and 6 are properties of the **driver**, not the translator: on
122	cancellation and on a transport error the translator is never called at all.
123	
124	More decisively, **SMA-531 was a driver defect.** Anthropic's translator
125	correctly buffered the stop reason; `model.rs:113` was a bare `None => return`
126	with no flush — and the crate had no `finish()` for a harness to call in the
127	first place (SMA-531's design doc, lines 20-21: "The crate's only `fn finish*`
128	is `finish_or_error` … that the driver never calls"). A harness that supplies
129	its own loop would have gone green against that exact defect. That is the
130	"conformance suite that cannot fail" failure mode the acceptance criteria name.
131	
132	The six drivers are *similar* but not identical, and the differences matter for
133	fixture design:
134	
135	- `openai/backend/responses.rs:70` — `None => return`, **no flush at all**.
136	- `gemini/src/model.rs:149-158` and `litellm/src/model.rs:163-166` — a `[DONE]`
137	  arm that flushes and returns, *plus* a separate EOF arm that also flushes.
138	  Two distinct terminal paths, which is what makes S2 non-vacuous for them.
139	- `bedrock/src/model.rs:102-124` — matches `Result<Option<_>, _>` from a
140	  channel receiver, not `Option<Result<_, _>>` from a stream.
141	- `gemini/src/model.rs:170-174` — returns mid-`consume` on the first `Err`.
142	
143	The cost of the Model boundary is per-subject wire fixtures. That cost is
144	accepted.
145	
146	## 5. Architecture
147	
148	New workspace member `tests/provider-stream-conformance`, package name
149	`paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance`, mirroring
150	`tests/runtime-http-conformance`:
151	
152	```
153	tests/provider-stream-conformance/
154	├── Cargo.toml            version = "0.0.0", publish = false, [lints] workspace = true
155	├── src/lib.rs            Scenario, Outcome, checker, PacedServer, non-conformant fakes
156	│                         deps: paigasus-helikon-core, async-trait, futures-util,
157	│                               tokio, hyper, hyper-util, http-body-util
158	├── tests/conformance.rs  registers the six subjects, runs the table
159	│                         dev-deps: all five provider crates
160	└── fixtures/             per-subject wire scripts
161	```
162	
163	Three registration chores that are easy to miss:
164	
165	- `Cargo.toml:3` is `members = ["crates/*", "tests/runtime-http-conformance"]` —
166	  the `tests/` entries are **enumerated, not globbed**. Add the new path.
167	- `release-plz.toml` gets a `publish = false` / `release = false` block,
168	  matching the two existing internal members.
169	- `scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh:29-30` iterates every `cargo metadata
170	  --no-deps` package with only `paigasus-helikon-cli` excluded, and the
171	  precedent sets `[lints] workspace = true`. So every `pub` item in `src/lib.rs`
172	  — `Scenario`, `Outcome`, `assert_conforms`, the fakes — **needs `///` docs**
173	  or the required `docs` and `doc-coverage` gates fail.
174	
175	**The dependency arrow points one way: suite → providers.** No provider crate
176	depends on the suite, so the dev-dependency cycle that deadlocked release-plz in
177	SMA-326 cannot arise. This is the main reason to prefer the
178	`runtime-http-conformance` precedent over the `sessions-testkit` one the ticket
179	names — `sessions-testkit` *is* dev-depended by its three backends, which is
180	exactly the cycle shape.
181	
182	Placing it under `tests/` also leaves the crate roster, the facade and every
183	README untouched. `docs/book/src/getting-started/workspace-layout.md` scopes its
184	"21" to `crates/` (there are exactly 21 directories there, and
185	`runtime-http-conformance` already sits outside the count), so that sentence
186	stays true and needs no edit.
187	
188	### 5.1 The seam
189	
190	`src/lib.rs` knows nothing about any provider:
191	
192	```rust
193	pub enum Scenario { /* §6 */ }
194	
195	/// What a subject did with a scenario. Declining is a first-class outcome with
196	/// a mandatory reason, not an `Option` a caller can silently treat as a skip.
197	pub enum Outcome {
198	    Served {
199	        stream: BoxStream<'static, Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
200	        /// Fires once the client has observably consumed the gate event.
201	        /// Present only for the cancellation scenarios. §6.1.
202	        gate: Option<GateHandle>,
203	    },
204	    /// The wire shape cannot physically occur for this provider.
205	    Declined(&'static str),
206	}
207	
208	#[async_trait]
209	pub trait StreamUnderTest {
210	    /// e.g. "openai/chat". Used in failure output and the decline set.
211	    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
212	
213	    /// Whether this subject's fixture for `scenario` encodes a stop reason.
214	    /// Cross-checked against the suite's own expectation — §6.2.
215	    fn encodes_stop_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> bool;
216	
217	    /// The tool name this subject's S6/S7 fixture declares, for the §7.1 floor.
218	    fn fixture_tool_name(&self) -> &'static str;
219	
220	    async fn stream(&self, scenario: Scenario, cancel: CancellationToken) -> Outcome;
221	}
222	
223	pub async fn assert_conforms(subject: &impl StreamUnderTest);
224	```
225	
226	### 5.2 The paced server
227	
228	wiremock writes the whole body in a single `set_body_raw`, so there is no pacing
229	to interrupt. `litellm/tests/cancellation.rs:3-5` documents this as the reason a
230	true mid-stream cancel goes untested, and OpenAI's tests carry the same note.
231	That limitation makes assertion 5 untestable in any meaningful sense:
232	cancel-*before*-response is satisfied trivially by any implementation.
233	
234	**The server is built on `hyper` 1.11 + `hyper-util` + `http-body-util`**, not a
235	hand-rolled `TcpListener`. A raw listener must also drain the request body
236	before responding (or a larger request races an RST), handle `Expect:
237	100-continue`, and manage keep-alive and protocol negotiation — none of which
238	serve the design, and all of which are failure modes that would present as
239	provider bugs. A `service_fn` with a channel-backed body gives correct chunked
240	framing for free and, critically, an **abortable** body that surfaces reliably
241	as an `Err` in reqwest, `async-openai` and the smithy client.
242	
243	The server emits a `Vec<Vec<u8>>` of chunks with a release gate between them.
244	Being byte-oriented rather than SSE-oriented, one server serves all five crates:
245	`text/event-stream` for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and LiteLLM, and
246	`application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` frames for Bedrock.
247	
248	Reachability: `base_url()` on OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and LiteLLM;
249	`SdkConfig::endpoint_url` plus static test credentials on Bedrock (unproven —
250	§11).
251	
252	`hyper`, `hyper-util`, `http-body-util` and `aws-smithy-eventstream` are all
253	already in `Cargo.lock` transitively, but "in the graph" is not "a dependency":
254	using them directly requires new `[workspace.dependencies]` pins per CLAUDE.md's
255	single-source-of-truth rule, and each adds a Dependabot surface.
256	
257	## 6. Scenarios
258	
259	| # | Scenario | Wire script | Asserts |
260	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
261	| S1 | `CleanStop` | deltas → stop-reason chunk → **usage chunk** → terminator → clean EOF | 1, 2, 3 |
262	| S2 | `TruncatedAfterStopReason` | deltas → stop reason observed → body ends cleanly, no terminator | 3 |
263	| S3 | `TruncatedMidGeneration` | deltas → body ends cleanly, no stop reason ever | 4 |
264	| S4a | `ErrorMidGeneration` | deltas → body aborted, no stop reason | 6, 1 |
265	| S4b | `ErrorAfterStopReason` | deltas → **stop reason observed** → body aborted | 6, 1 |
266	| S5a | `CancelMidGeneration` | deltas → gate → token fires, no stop reason | 5 |
267	| S5b | `CancelAfterStopReason` | deltas → **stop reason observed** → gate → token fires | 5 |
268	| S6 | `FragmentedToolName` | tool-call deltas, name split across ≥2 fragments | 7, 1 |
269	| S7 | `ToolCallCleanStop` | one complete tool call → tool-use stop reason → terminator | 1, 3, 7 |
270	
271	**S4 and S5 are each split, and the split is the point.** The single-scenario
272	versions in the earlier draft could not fail. With no stop reason buffered, a
273	driver that *wrongly* flushes `finish()` on the error arm emits no `Finish`
274	either — there is nothing to flush — so assertion 6 passed for correct and
275	broken code alike. S4b supplies the buffered stop reason that makes the
276	assertion bite. This is not hypothetical: SMA-522's design doc records
277	`Transport / parse error after finish chunk` as a changed path, and SMA-531's
278	design doc (lines 78-81) names "SMA-533's acceptance clause 6" as its reason for
279	leaving Anthropic's dirty-cut arm unguarded. **This ticket is the one that was
280	supposed to guard it.** The same reasoning splits S5.
281	
282	**S1 must place usage *after* the stop reason.** That is the real OpenAI wire
283	order. SMA-522 went undetected precisely because the fixtures encoded a shape
284	that does not occur.
285	
286	**S3 and S4a differ only in how the body ends.** S3 completes the body cleanly:
287	the client sees EOF mid-generation, no stop reason was observed, no `Finish` may
288	be emitted. S4a aborts it: the client sees a truncated body, yields `Err`, and
289	still emits no `Finish`. `async-openai`'s pump treats a clean EOF as `None`
290	rather than an error (`client.rs:842-865`), so S3 will not be mis-reported as
291	S4a.
292	
293	**Provenance rule.** Every fixture is transcribed from captured or
294	already-committed traffic — the repo has fixture directories for LiteLLM
295	(captured against 1.97/1.98 with the image digest recorded in the file header),
296	Anthropic and OpenAI — and never invented from vendor documentation. Applying
297	that rule to this spec's own first draft: S6 originally specified "id resolving
298	after the first fragment", which **no capture in the repo supports**. The one
299	committed capture of a fragmented name,
300	`litellm/tests/fixtures/tool_call_stream_fragmented_name.txt`, states in its
301	header that the fragments "BOTH arrive after the id". S6 uses the committed
302	shape; the late-id variant is dropped.
303	
304	### 6.1 The cancellation gate
305	
306	A cancellation test without a happens-before edge is sleep-and-hope —
307	`openai/tests/cancellation.rs:88-93` explicitly refuses to ship one, on the
308	grounds that it "would assert whatever the scheduler happened to do".
309	
310	The stop-reason chunk itself is not usable as that edge: `openai/chat` buffers
311	`finish_reason` silently (`backend/chat.rs:290-314`), as does LiteLLM. So S5b's
312	script places an **observable** event after the stop reason and before the gate
313	— a usage chunk for `openai/chat`, `litellm` and `gemini`; for Anthropic
314	`message_delta` already emits `Usage` from the same event
315	(`anthropic/stream.rs:161-181`). The harness blocks on observing that event,
316	then fires the token. `GateHandle` (§5.1) is what the subject hands back to let
317	the harness release the remaining chunks.
318	
319	### 6.2 Declines, and why they are cross-checked
320	
321	| Subject | S1 | S2 | S3 | S4a | S4b | S5a | S5b | S6 | S7 |
322	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
323	| `openai/chat` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
324	| `litellm` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
325	| `anthropic` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ a | ✓ |
326	| `gemini` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ a | ✓ |
327	| `bedrock` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ b | ✗ a | ✓ |
328	| `openai/responses` | ✓ | ✗ c | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ c | ✓ | ✗ c | ✗ a | ✓ |
329	
330	- **a** — the tool name arrives whole in a single `content_block_start` /
331	  `functionCall` / `toolUse` / `output_item.added` event. There is no fragment
332	  to split.
333	- **b** — the window between "stop reason buffered" and "`Finish` emitted" lies
334	  strictly between `MessageStop` and `Metadata`, with no event emitted in
335	  between (`bedrock/src/stream.rs:214-242`), so no gate edge exists.
336	- **c** — `terminal_events` builds `Usage` and `Finish` from one upstream event
337	  (`backend/responses.rs:454-489`), so "stop reason observed but no `Finish`
338	  yet" is not a reachable state.
339	
340	Every assertion still runs for every subject: 5 via S5a where S5b is declined,
341	6 via S4a where S4b is declined, 7 via S7 where S6 is declined.
342	
343	**The stop-reason condition is cross-checked, not merely declared.** Assertions
344	3 and 4 are conditioned on whether a stop reason was observed, and the harness
345	cannot infer that from the emitted events — a provider wrongly suppressing
346	`Finish` looks identical to one that correctly never saw a stop reason. The
347	earlier draft declared the condition suite-side while each subject supplied its
348	own bytes, with nothing reconciling the two; a mis-transcribed fixture would
349	then make assertion 3 pass vacuously. So `encodes_stop_reason` (§5.1) is
350	declared per subject and **asserted against the suite's own expectation for that
351	scenario**, and S1/S7 additionally assert the specific `FinishReason` the
352	fixture declares.
353	
354	## 7. Assertions
355	
356	1. **`Finish`-terminated.** Nothing follows `Finish` — no `ModelEvent` and no
357	   `Err`; at most one `Finish` is emitted.
358	2. **`Usage` precedes `Finish`** when present.
359	3. **EOF after an observed stop reason emits `Finish`.**
360	4. **No stop reason observed ⇒ no `Finish`.**
361	5. **Cancellation emits no `Finish`.**
362	6. **A mid-stream error emits no `Finish`.**
363	7. **Exactly one `ToolCallDelta` per observed `call_id` carries `Some(name)`,
364	   and that name equals the fixture's declared tool name.**
365	
366	**Assertion 7 says "exactly", not "at most".** The ticket's wording is "at most
367	one", which a translator that drops the name entirely satisfies — and that is
368	precisely SMA-547's bug class. `openai/backend/chat.rs:338-349` states the
369	stakes: the name flush "is a correctness requirement, not a diagnostic: … a name
370	never emitted becomes an empty name that resolves to no tool."
371	
372	**Assertion 2 is subsumed by assertion 1.** If nothing may follow `Finish`, any
373	`Usage` present necessarily precedes it. Both are kept, but 2 exists for its
374	diagnostic, not for coverage.
375	
376	**Violation classification is ordered**, because the rules overlap and §8 demands
377	a *specific* violation. The checker reports the first match in this order:
378	
379	1. a second `Finish` → `DuplicateFinish` (assertion 1)
380	2. a `Usage` after `Finish` → `UsageAfterFinish` (assertion 2)
381	3. any other event or `Err` after `Finish` → `EventAfterFinish` (assertion 1)
382	4. assertions 3–7 in numeric order
383	
384	### 7.1 Vacuous passes
385	
386	A stream that emits nothing satisfies "ends with `Finish`" trivially, and a
387	miswired adapter serving the wrong fixture would pass every assertion by
388	producing nothing. Each scenario therefore carries a positive-evidence floor,
389	checked *before* the assertions run:
390	
391	- S1–S5b must yield ≥ 1 `TokenDelta`.
392	- S6 and S7 must yield ≥ 1 `ToolCallDelta`, of which **exactly one carries
393	  `Some(name)` equal to `fixture_tool_name()`**.
394	- S1 and S7 must yield exactly one `Finish`, with the `FinishReason` the fixture
395	  declares.
396	- S4a and S4b must yield exactly one `Err`.
397	
398	Every scenario also runs under a `tokio::time::timeout`. A subject whose stream
399	never terminates is a real bug this suite should catch, and without the timeout
400	it would hang `cargo test` rather than fail it.
401	
402	## 8. Proving the suite can fail
403	
404	Verifying by hand once leaves nothing behind, so it is built in. `src/fakes.rs`
405	ships ten non-conforming fake event sequences (plus `Fake::Conforming`, which
406	violates none), each violating exactly one rule, and the crate's own unit
407	tests assert the checker rejects each **with the classification named in
408	§7**. These are deliberately *not* `Model` implementations: each fake builds
409	its `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` in memory and calls `classify`
410	directly, so no server, no transport and no provider crate is on this path —
411	a fake can never be rejected by a floor instead of the classification it is
412	written to trigger (`src/fakes.rs`'s module doc explains and justifies this):
413	
414	| Fake | Expected classification | Replicates |
415	| --- | --- | --- |
416	| `EventAfterFinish` | `EventAfterFinish` | — |
417	| `ErrAfterFinish` | `EventAfterFinish` | — |
418	| `DoubleFinish` | `DuplicateFinish` | — |
419	| `UsageAfterFinish` | `UsageAfterFinish` | SMA-522 |
420	| `NoFinishAfterStopReason` | assertion 3 | SMA-531 |
421	| `FinishOnTruncation` | assertion 4 | — |
422	| `FinishOnCancel` | assertion 5 | — |
423	| `FinishAfterError` | assertion 6 | — |
424	| `TwoNamedDeltas` | assertion 7 | SMA-550 |
425	
426	A tenth case, `NoNamedDelta`, guards the "exactly one" tightening: a translator
427	that emits tool-call deltas but never a name must fail assertion 7.
428	
429	This runs on every CI run, so the suite cannot silently decay into one that
430	always passes.
431	
432	## 9. Handling discovered failures
433	
434	Default: **every subject passes every assertion when the PR merges.** Small,
435	obvious defects are fixed here and noted in the PR body.
436	
437	If a discovered defect needs a genuine design decision rather than a small fix,
438	implementation **stops and surfaces it** rather than deciding unilaterally. Only
439	then does it become an exception: a filed Linear issue, an
440	`#[ignore = "SMA-XXX: <one line>"]`, and a row in the exception table.
441	
442	### 9.1 The decline set is pinned
443	
444	`Outcome::Declined` would otherwise be a second escape hatch with none of that
445	rigor — a future engineer facing a red assertion could convert it to
446	`Declined("wire shape cannot occur")` in one line and keep CI green.
447	
448	So the expected declines are pinned as a `const DECLINED: &[(&str, Scenario, &str)]`
449	in `src/declines.rs` — subject, scenario, and the reason string, so a reworded
450	reason is drift too — exactly matching §6.2, and the suite **fails when the observed
451	decline set differs in either direction** — an unexpected decline *and* an
452	expected decline that stopped happening. Adding or removing one then requires a
453	reviewed diff to a table, not a string literal in a match arm.
454	
455	## 10. Documentation changes
456	
457	All doc-only. **Four** `-core` sites, not three: `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`
458	carries the positional wording twice, once on the variant and once on the
459	`name` field.
460	
461	| Site | Change |
462	| --- | --- |
463	| `core/src/model.rs` — `Model::invoke` | Add the emission rule (exact text below). |
464	| `core/src/model.rs:180-182` — `ToolCallDelta` **variant** doc | "`name` is `Some` on the first delta for a given `call_id`, then `None` on subsequent deltas" → completeness wording. |
465	| `core/src/model.rs:186` — `ToolCallDelta.name` **field** doc | "Tool name; `Some` on the first delta only." → completeness wording. |
466	| `core/src/agent.rs:384` — `AgentEvent::ToolCallDelta.name` | Same replacement. |
467	| `bedrock/src/stream.rs:14` and `:439` | **SMA-532.** Both assert `Usage` "must precede" `Finish` per the ordering contract. Only `Finish` is positionally constrained. Comment text only; Bedrock's implementation is correct and is not touched. |
468	| `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md:57` | Describes `Finish { reason }` as terminal; gains the emission rule, so prose and test cannot drift. |
469	
470	**Exact text, `Model::invoke`:**
471	
472	> Implementations MUST emit `Finish` at end-of-stream when a stop reason was
473	> observed, and MUST NOT emit it on truncation with no stop reason observed, on
474	> cancellation, or after a mid-stream error.
475	
476	**Exact text, all three `ToolCallDelta.name` sites:**
477	
478	> `Some` exactly once per `call_id`, on the first delta for which the provider
479	> can establish the name is complete, and `None` on every other delta. When
480	> `Some`, the value is the whole name so far as the provider can determine — a
481	> provider receiving the name in fragments MUST buffer and concatenate them, and
482	> MUST NOT emit a name it can detect is still incomplete.
483	
484	The **"can detect" qualifier is load-bearing** and must survive verbatim: a
485	single delta carrying both `{"name":"get_","arguments":"{\"ci"}` flushes
486	`Some("get_")`, a partial no translator can rule out without abandoning
487	streaming names entirely. An unqualified "never emit a partial" would make the
488	two providers SMA-547 just fixed non-conformant against a contract added in the
489	same change.
490	
491	**This tightens a public trait's contract for third-party implementors** under a
492	patch bump. It is doc-only and semver-compatible, but the CHANGELOG entry and
493	the book page should describe it as a contract clarification, not a doc tweak.
494	
495	No crate `README.md` changes: the suite is not a published crate, and no
496	published crate's public API, feature set or install story changes.
497	
498	## 11. Risks, fallbacks, and sequencing
499	
500	Bedrock and the paced server carry every unproven assumption and no existing
501	coverage (§1.1), so they are built **first**. If they cannot be made to work the
502	design changes shape, and that must be known before five subjects are written
503	against it.
504	
505	| Risk | Fallback |
506	| --- | --- |
507	| SigV4 against a local plain-HTTP endpoint with static credentials is unverified. The smithy TLS builder is `.https_or_http()` but also calls `.enable_http2()`. | Proven by execution in the first task, per this repo's rule that wire behaviour is verified against a running server rather than read from docs. If it fails: `StaticReplayClient` covering **S1, S2, S3, S6, S7 only** — a whole-body replay client cannot abort a body, so S4a/S4b and S5a/S5b are declined for Bedrock with reasons. Note that `StaticReplayClient` sits behind `aws-smithy-runtime`'s `test-util` feature, which `Cargo.toml:142` does not currently enable, so this also shifts feature unification under `--all-features`. |
508	| Hand-built eventstream frames may decode as `Unknown` if `:event-type` must match the union member name exactly or `:content-type` must be `application/json`. `bedrock/src/stream.rs:244-246` has a forward-compat catch-all that **silently drops** unknown variants, so this would present as every Bedrock scenario failing its positive-evidence floor — looking like a translator bug. | Assert the floor first, so the failure is attributed correctly; validate one frame round-trips before writing the rest. |
509	| Bedrock's registration is "roughly twenty lines" for the other five subjects but well past it here: `SdkConfig` + `endpoint_url` + test credentials, a frame writer with `:message-type` / `:event-type` / `:content-type` headers, and per-event JSON payloads. | Budgeted as its own task. |
510	| Bedrock's eventstream fixtures are **binary**. A `*.txt text eol=lf` glob over them would silently corrupt them. | Add an explicit `binary` (`-text`) rule for the Bedrock fixture directory in `.gitattributes`, alongside the existing `text eol=lf` rule for SSE fixtures (`.gitattributes:3-15`). |
511	| The suite surfaces failures the ticket did not predict | §9. |
512	
513	## 12. Out of scope, with follow-ups to file
514	
515	- **Unifying the `finish()` return shape** (§2.2). Carry the table verbatim.
516	- **`openai/chat`'s same-`id`-different-`index` shape** (§2.1) — real, unobserved
517	  from any backend, uncovered by this suite because no capture exists. The
518	  in-source comment already says "closing it needs its own ticket"; file it.
519	- **`paigasus_helikon_evals::MockModel` ignores its `_cancel` argument**
520	  (`evals/src/mock.rs:48-62`), so a `Model` shipped by this workspace violates
521	  the *existing* written cancellation clause and would fail assertion 5. Not a
522	  provider, so out of this suite's scope — but it is a conformance defect in
523	  code we own, found while writing this spec. File it.
524	- **SMA-548** (Anthropic `finish_or_error` reason-mapping rows with no
525	  assertion) — one crate's mapping table, not cross-provider ordering; the
526	  ticket records it as not a duplicate.
527	- **`ReasoningDelta` ordering, parallel tool calls, zero-argument tool calls.**
528	  No scenario covers them. `Err` terminality *is* covered, folded into
529	  assertion 1.
530	- Any behavioural change to a provider beyond fixing a conformance failure the
531	  suite surfaces.
532	
533	## 13. Acceptance criteria
534	
535	1. Every (subject, scenario) pair either runs or is `Declined` with a reason
536	   drawn from the pinned `DECLINED` set (§9.1), and the suite fails if the
537	   observed decline set differs from it in either direction.
538	2. Every assertion 1–7 runs for all six subjects, via the substitutions in
539	   §6.2 where a scenario is declined.
540	3. Each assertion has a non-conformant fake that the checker rejects with the
541	   classification named in §7, asserted in the suite's own unit tests (§8) —
542	   including `NoNamedDelta` for the "exactly one" tightening.
543	4. Every scenario enforces its positive-evidence floor and runs under a timeout
544	   (§7.1).
545	5. The four `-core` doc sites, the two Bedrock comment sites and the book page
546	   carry the wording quoted verbatim in §10.
547	6. No `version` field is edited anywhere (§2.3).
548	7. Follow-up tickets from §12 are filed and linked in the PR body.
549	8. The full CI gate list in CLAUDE.md passes: `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`,
550	   `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo doc` with
551	   `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`, doc coverage, and `mdbook build docs/book`.
552
