1	//! Fake model streams that prove the checker can fail.
2	//!
3	//! Each non-conforming variant violates exactly one rule, and the tests below
4	//! assert that [`classify`] rejects it with the classification the design spec
5	//! names for that rule (§8). This runs on every CI run, so the suite cannot
6	//! silently decay into one that always passes.
7	//!
8	//! These fakes exercise the **checker**, not the HTTP path: `run` builds the
9	//! event vector in memory and classifies it, so no server, no transport and no
10	//! provider crate is involved. The floors and the decline cross-check in
11	//! `assert_conforms` are therefore not on this path — a fake can never be
12	//! rejected by a floor instead of by the classification it is written to
13	//! trigger.
14	
15	use crate::{classify, Scenario, Violation};
16	use paigasus_helikon_core::{FinishReason, ModelError, ModelEvent};
17	
18	/// The tool name every tool-bearing fake declares.
19	pub(crate) const TOOL_NAME: &str = "get_weather";
20	
21	/// The `call_id` every tool-bearing fake uses. The tests pin the reported
22	/// violation against this exact string, so it is shared rather than repeated.
23	const CALL_ID: &str = "c1";
24	
25	/// A stream shape that violates exactly one rule — plus [`Fake::Conforming`],
26	/// which violates none.
27	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
28	pub enum Fake {
29	    /// A `TokenDelta` after `Finish` (assertion 1).
30	    EventAfterFinish,
31	    /// An `Err` after `Finish` (assertion 1).
32	    ErrAfterFinish,
33	    /// Two `Finish` events (assertion 1).
34	    DoubleFinish,
35	    /// A `Usage` after `Finish` — the SMA-522 shape (assertion 2).
36	    UsageAfterFinish,
37	    /// End-of-stream after an observed stop reason with no `Finish` — the
38	    /// SMA-531 shape (assertion 3).
39	    NoFinishAfterStopReason,
40	    /// A `Finish` although no stop reason was observed (assertion 4).
41	    FinishOnTruncation,
42	    /// A `Finish` after cancellation (assertion 5).
43	    FinishOnCancel,
44	    /// A `Finish` after a mid-stream error (assertion 6).
45	    FinishAfterError,
46	    /// Two name-bearing deltas for one `call_id` — the SMA-550 shape
47	    /// (assertion 7).
48	    TwoNamedDeltas,
49	    /// Tool-call deltas that never carry a name, which is what the "exactly
50	    /// one" tightening of assertion 7 exists to catch.
51	    NoNamedDelta,
52	    /// A sequence that satisfies every assertion for the given scenario.
53	    Conforming,
54	}
55	
56	impl Fake {
57	    /// Build this fake's event sequence for `scenario` and classify it.
58	    ///
59	    /// `cancelled` is derived from the scenario rather than passed in, so a
60	    /// fake can never be tested under a cancellation flag that contradicts the
61	    /// script it is emitting.
62	    pub async fn run(self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<Violation> {
63	        classify(
64	            &self.events(scenario),
65	            scenario,
66	            crate::is_cancel_scenario(scenario),
67	        )
68	    }
69	
70	    /// The event sequence this fake emits for `scenario`.
71	    ///
72	    /// Every non-conforming variant is built by perturbing
73	    /// [`Fake::Conforming`]'s sequence for the *same* scenario, so each fake
74	    /// differs from a passing stream by exactly the one rule it violates —
75	    /// there is no hand-written sequence that could accidentally break a
76	    /// second rule and be rejected for the wrong reason.
77	    fn events(self, scenario: Scenario) -> Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>> {
78	        let mut events = conforming(scenario);
79	        match self {
80	            Fake::Conforming => {}
81	            Fake::EventAfterFinish => events.push(token("trailing")),
82	            Fake::ErrAfterFinish => events.push(Err(ModelError::Unavailable)),
83	            // The scenarios these three are tested under differ, and so does
84	            // the rule each one breaks: appending a `Finish` to a stream that
85	            // already has one breaks assertion 1, to a truncated one breaks
86	            // assertion 4, to a cancelled one breaks assertion 5, and to an
87	            // errored one breaks assertion 6.
88	            Fake::DoubleFinish
89	            | Fake::FinishOnTruncation
90	            | Fake::FinishOnCancel
91	            | Fake::FinishAfterError => events.push(finish(scenario)),
92	            Fake::UsageAfterFinish => {
93	                events.retain(|e| !matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::Usage { .. })));
94	                events.push(usage());
95	            }
96	            Fake::NoFinishAfterStopReason => {
97	                events.retain(|e| !matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::Finish { .. })));
98	            }
99	            Fake::TwoNamedDeltas => {
100	                // Split the name across both deltas instead of emitting it
101	                // once, leaving everything else about the sequence intact.
102	                replace_tool_deltas(
103	                    &mut events,
104	                    &[
105	                        (Some("get_"), "{\"city\":"),
106	                        (Some("weather"), "\"Berlin\"}"),
107	                    ],
108	                );
109	            }
110	            Fake::NoNamedDelta => {
111	                replace_tool_deltas(&mut events, &[(None, "{\"city\":\"Berlin\"}")]);
112	            }
113	        }
114	        events
115	    }
116	}
117	
118	/// The sequence a conforming subject emits for `scenario`.
119	///
120	/// A `Usage` and a `Finish` appear only when the scenario lets the translator
121	/// observe a stop reason *and* the stream is neither cancelled nor errored —
122	/// withholding `Finish` is what the contract requires in those two cases.
123	pub(crate) fn conforming(scenario: Scenario) -> Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>> {
124	    let mut events = vec![token("hi")];
125	
126	    if matches!(
127	        scenario,
128	        Scenario::FragmentedToolName
129	            | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
130	            | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
131	    ) {
132	        events.push(tool(Some(TOOL_NAME), "{\"city\":"));
133	        events.push(tool(None, "\"Berlin\"}"));
134	    }
135	    if scenario == Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop {
136	        // The position record of the tool call, scoped to the fake call.
137	        events.push(Ok(ModelEvent::ProviderData {
138	            provider: "test".into(),
139	            call_id: Some(CALL_ID.into()),
140	            data: serde_json::json!({ "kind": "tool_use" }),
141	        }));
142	    }
143	
144	    let errored = matches!(
145	        scenario,
146	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
147	    );
148	    let cancelled = matches!(
149	        scenario,
150	        Scenario::CancelMidGeneration | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
151	    );
152	    if scenario.expects_stop_reason() && !errored {
153	        // `CancelAfterStopReason` gets the `Usage` but not the `Finish`. That
154	        // is not a detail: its script places a usage chunk *after* the
155	        // stop-reason chunk and gates on it, so a conforming subject really
156	        // does emit one before the token fires — and the harness's floor looks
157	        // for exactly that to tell S5b from a gate placed one chunk too early.
158	        // Withholding `Finish` is what the contract requires of a cancelled
159	        // stream, and of an errored one.
160	        events.push(usage());
161	        if !cancelled {
162	            events.push(finish(scenario));
163	        }
164	    }
165	
166	    if matches!(
167	        scenario,
168	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
169	    ) {
170	        events.push(Err(ModelError::Unavailable));
171	    }
172	
173	    events
174	}
175	
176	/// Swap every `ToolCallDelta` in `events` for `deltas`, in place, keeping the
177	/// position of the first one. Used to perturb only the tool-call half of a
178	/// conforming sequence.
179	fn replace_tool_deltas(
180	    events: &mut Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
181	    deltas: &[(Option<&str>, &str)],
182	) {
183	    let at = events
184	        .iter()
185	        .position(|e| matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta { .. })))
186	        .expect("a tool-call fake must be run under a tool-call scenario");
187	    events.retain(|e| !matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta { .. })));
188	    for (offset, (name, args)) in deltas.iter().enumerate() {
189	        events.insert(at + offset, tool(*name, args));
190	    }
191	}
192	
193	/// A text delta.
194	fn token(text: &str) -> Result<ModelEvent, ModelError> {
195	    Ok(ModelEvent::TokenDelta { text: text.into() })
196	}
197	
198	/// A usage snapshot.
199	fn usage() -> Result<ModelEvent, ModelError> {
200	    Ok(ModelEvent::Usage {
201	        input_tokens: 7,
202	        output_tokens: 3,
203	        cached_input_tokens: None,
204	        reasoning_tokens: None,
205	    })
206	}
207	
208	/// The terminal event, carrying the reason the scenario's script would encode.
209	fn finish(scenario: Scenario) -> Result<ModelEvent, ModelError> {
210	    Ok(ModelEvent::Finish {
211	        reason: match scenario {
212	            Scenario::FragmentedToolName
213	            | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
214	            | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => FinishReason::ToolCalls,
215	            _ => FinishReason::Stop,
216	        },
217	    })
218	}
219	
220	/// One tool-call delta for [`CALL_ID`].
221	fn tool(name: Option<&str>, args_delta: &str) -> Result<ModelEvent, ModelError> {
222	    Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta {
223	        call_id: CALL_ID.into(),
224	        name: name.map(str::to_owned),
225	        args_delta: args_delta.into(),
226	    })
227	}
228	
229	#[cfg(test)]
230	mod tests {
231	    use super::*;
232	
233	    /// Every fake must be rejected with its own classification. A suite whose
234	    /// checker cannot fail is the exact failure mode that let the OpenAI bug
235	    /// ship past green fixtures.
236	    #[tokio::test]
237	    async fn every_fake_is_rejected_with_its_classification() {
238	        let cases: Vec<(Fake, Scenario, Violation)> = vec![
239	            (
240	                Fake::EventAfterFinish,
241	                Scenario::CleanStop,
242	                Violation::EventAfterFinish,
243	            ),
244	            (
245	                Fake::ErrAfterFinish,
246	                Scenario::CleanStop,
247	                Violation::EventAfterFinish,
248	            ),
249	            (
250	                Fake::DoubleFinish,
251	                Scenario::CleanStop,
252	                Violation::DuplicateFinish,
253	            ),
254	            (
255	                Fake::UsageAfterFinish,
256	                Scenario::CleanStop,
257	                Violation::UsageAfterFinish,
258	            ),
259	            (
260	                Fake::NoFinishAfterStopReason,
261	                Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason,
262	                Violation::MissingFinish,
263	            ),
264	            (
265	                Fake::FinishOnTruncation,
266	                Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration,
267	                Violation::FinishOnTruncation,
268	            ),
269	            (
270	                Fake::FinishOnCancel,
271	                Scenario::CancelMidGeneration,
272	                Violation::FinishOnCancel,
273	            ),
274	            (
275	                Fake::FinishAfterError,
276	                Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason,
277	                Violation::FinishAfterError,
278	            ),
279	            (
280	                Fake::TwoNamedDeltas,
281	                Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop,
282	                Violation::ToolNameNotExactlyOnce {
283	                    call_id: "c1".into(),
284	                    count: 2,
285	                },
286	            ),
287	            (
288	                Fake::NoNamedDelta,
289	                Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop,
290	                Violation::ToolNameNotExactlyOnce {
291	                    call_id: "c1".into(),
292	                    count: 0,
293	                },
294	            ),
295	        ];
296	
297	        for (fake, scenario, expected) in cases {
298	            let observed = fake.run(scenario).await;
299	            assert_eq!(
300	                observed,
301	                Some(expected.clone()),
302	                "{fake:?} on {scenario:?} must be rejected as {expected:?}"
303	            );
304	        }
305	    }
306	
307	    /// The conforming fake must pass every scenario it serves.
308	    #[tokio::test]
309	    async fn the_conforming_fake_passes() {
310	        for scenario in Scenario::ALL {
311	            assert_eq!(Fake::Conforming.run(*scenario).await, None, "{scenario:?}");
312	        }
313	    }
314	
315	    /// What a subject serving `conforming(scenario)` would declare as its
316	    /// fixture's `FinishReason`.
317	    ///
318	    /// Written out independently of [`finish`] rather than read back out of the
319	    /// sequence: the floor checks that the declaration and the emitted event
320	    /// agree, and deriving one from the other would make that check tautological.
321	    fn declared_finish_reason(scenario: Scenario) -> Option<FinishReason> {
322	        match scenario {
323	            Scenario::CleanStop | Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => Some(FinishReason::Stop),
324	            Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => {
325	                Some(FinishReason::ToolCalls)
326	            }
327	            _ => None,
328	        }
329	    }
330	
331	    /// The floors are the harness's own anti-vacuity guard, and the fakes never
332	    /// reach them — so pin here that a conforming sequence would also clear
333	    /// them. Without this, a floor that rejects every well-formed stream would
334	    /// only be discovered by Task 7's first subject.
335	    #[test]
336	    fn the_conforming_fake_clears_every_floor() {
337	        for scenario in Scenario::ALL {
338	            assert_eq!(
339	                crate::floor_violation(
340	                    *scenario,
341	                    &conforming(*scenario),
342	                    TOOL_NAME,
343	                    declared_finish_reason(*scenario),
344	                ),
345	                None,
346	                "{scenario:?}"
347	            );
348	        }
349	    }
350	}

1	//! The registered conformance subjects.
2	//!
3	//! Each subject in this file serves its own wire bytes through the crate's
4	//! paced HTTP server and hands back the stream from its real `Model::invoke`,
5	//! so every assertion in `assert_conforms` is made about production driver and
6	//! production translator code — never about a reimplementation of either.
7	//!
8	//! ## Adding a subject
9	//!
10	//! One `mod <subject> { … }` per subject, holding its fixture helpers, its
11	//! `StreamUnderTest` impl and one `#[tokio::test]` that calls
12	//! `assert_conforms`. The module scoping is not cosmetic: it is what lets every
13	//! subject call its helpers `text_delta`, `script`, `request` and so on without
14	//! a per-subject prefix, and it keeps six subjects' worth of near-identical
15	//! names from colliding in one flat namespace.
16	//!
17	//! Two rules apply to every subject, and both exist because breaking them makes
18	//! a check pass without measuring anything:
19	//!
20	//! 1. **Decline reasons are literal strings**, copied by hand from
21	//!    `src/declines.rs`. A subject that looked its reasons up from `DECLINED`
22	//!    would satisfy that table's two-directional cross-check by construction,
23	//!    which is exactly the drift the table exists to catch.
24	//! 2. **`encodes_stop_reason` is measured from the bytes about to be served**,
25	//!    never restated from `Scenario::expects_stop_reason`. Restating it
26	//!    compares the harness's expectation with itself. See the Bedrock impl for
27	//!    what it catches.
28	
29	use paigasus_helikon_core::{
30	    CancellationToken, ContentPart, FinishReason, Item, Model, ModelRequest, ToolDef,
31	};
32	use paigasus_helikon_provider_stream_conformance::{
33	    assert_conforms, eventstream::frame, Ending, Outcome, PacedServer, Scenario, Script,
34	    StreamUnderTest,
35	};
36	use serde_json::json;
37	
38	/// The `Model::invoke` stream contract, checked against the Bedrock
39	/// `ConverseStream` provider.
40	///
41	/// # Fixture provenance
42	///
43	/// Bedrock is the one subject in this suite whose wire format is binary, and
44	/// the repo holds no captured Bedrock traffic to transcribe. So — as the task
45	/// brief directs when no capture exists — every event shape here is derived
46	/// from two sources inside the workspace, and from nothing else:
47	///
48	/// 1. **The translator's own match arms**, `providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs`.
49	///    Which `ConverseStreamOutput` variants matter, and what each one must
50	///    carry to produce a `ModelEvent`, is read off the arms that consume them:
51	///    `ContentBlockDelta`/`Text` to `TokenDelta`, `ContentBlockStart`/`ToolUse`
52	///    plus `ContentBlockDelta`/`ToolUse` to `ToolCallDelta`, `MessageStop` to
53	///    the buffered stop reason, `Metadata`/`usage` to `Usage` then `Finish`.
54	/// 2. **The vendored AWS Converse types** in `aws-sdk-bedrockruntime` 1.140.0.
55	///    Every JSON key below is the key that crate's own deserializer reads, and
56	///    every `:event-type` is the union member name its
57	///    `ConverseStreamOutputUnmarshaller` dispatches on
58	///    (`src/event_stream_serde.rs`). Per-shape references sit on each helper.
59	///
60	/// Nothing here is transcribed from vendor documentation, and no shape is
61	/// invented: a frame the SDK's decoder does not recognise is dropped silently
62	/// by the translator's forward-compat catch-all rather than rejected, so an
63	/// invented shape would present as a translator bug and not as a bad fixture.
64	///
65	/// # Why there are no `.bin` fixture files
66	///
67	/// A `vnd.amazon.eventstream` frame is a length-prefixed header block wrapped
68	/// in two CRC-32s, so a checked-in `.bin` would be neither reviewable nor
69	/// editable, and any byte edited by hand would fail its CRC rather than test
70	/// anything. `eventstream::frame` exists precisely to avoid that: it encodes
71	/// each fixture with the same encoder the SDK itself uses, so the bytes that
72	/// reach the wire are real while the fixture stays readable as JSON.
73	mod bedrock {
74	    use super::*;
75	
76	    /// The tool name every Bedrock tool fixture declares.
77	    const TOOL_NAME: &str = "get_weather";
78	
79	    /// `toolUseId` for the single tool call in the tool fixtures.
80	    ///
81	    /// Deliberately *not* claimed to match any real Bedrock id format: the SDK
82	    /// types this field as a plain `String` with no format constraint
83	    /// (`_tool_use_block_start.rs`: `pub tool_use_id: String`), and the
84	    /// translator copies it verbatim into `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta.call_id`
85	    /// (`stream.rs:116`), so nothing under test inspects its shape. The value
86	    /// is fixed and self-describing purely so failure output is stable and
87	    /// greppable.
88	    const TOOL_USE_ID: &str = "tooluse_conformance_0";
89	
90	    /// The `:event-type` value carried by the one event that encodes a stop
91	    /// reason. Used by [`Bedrock::encodes_stop_reason`] to measure a script.
92	    const MESSAGE_STOP_EVENT_TYPE: &str = "messageStop";
93	
94	    /// `messageStart`, which opens every Converse stream.
95	    ///
96	    /// The translator ignores it (`ConverseStreamOutput::MessageStart(_) => {}`);
97	    /// it is here because a real stream always sends it first, and a fixture
98	    /// that silently omitted the opening event would not be the stream it
99	    /// claims to be. Key: `role` (`shape_message_start_event.rs`), value from
100	    /// `ConversationRole` (`_conversation_role.rs`: `"assistant"`).
101	    fn message_start() -> Vec<u8> {
102	        frame("messageStart", &json!({ "role": "assistant" }))
103	    }
104	
105	    /// One text delta. `stream.rs`'s `ContentBlockDelta::Text` arm turns this
106	    /// into `ModelEvent::TokenDelta`.
107	    ///
108	    /// Keys: `contentBlockIndex` and `delta`
109	    /// (`shape_content_block_delta_event.rs`), with `text` the
110	    /// `ContentBlockDelta` union member (`shape_content_block_delta.rs`).
111	    fn text_delta(text: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
112	        frame(
113	            "contentBlockDelta",
114	            &json!({ "contentBlockIndex": 0, "delta": { "text": text } }),
115	        )
116	    }
117	
118	    /// `contentBlockStart` opening a tool-use block.
119	    ///
120	    /// The translator records the block's `call_id` and `name` here but emits
121	    /// nothing — the name-carrying `ToolCallDelta` comes with the *first* input
122	    /// delta. That is why `FragmentedToolName` is declined for this subject:
123	    /// the name arrives whole, in this one event.
124	    ///
125	    /// Keys: `contentBlockIndex` and `start`
126	    /// (`shape_content_block_start_event.rs`), `toolUse` the union member
127	    /// (`shape_content_block_start.rs`), and `toolUseId` / `name` inside it
128	    /// (`shape_tool_use_block_start.rs`).
129	    fn tool_use_start() -> Vec<u8> {
130	        frame(
131	            "contentBlockStart",
132	            &json!({
133	                "contentBlockIndex": 0,
134	                "start": { "toolUse": { "toolUseId": TOOL_USE_ID, "name": TOOL_NAME } }
135	            }),
136	        )
137	    }
138	
139	    /// One tool-argument delta. Bedrock streams tool input as a partial JSON
140	    /// string, so `input` is a string fragment and not an object.
141	    ///
142	    /// Keys: `delta.toolUse` (`shape_content_block_delta.rs`) with `input`
143	    /// (`shape_tool_use_block_delta.rs`).
144	    fn tool_use_delta(input: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
145	        frame(
146	            "contentBlockDelta",
147	            &json!({ "contentBlockIndex": 0, "delta": { "toolUse": { "input": input } } }),
148	        )
149	    }
150	
151	    /// `contentBlockStop`, which closes a content block. Ignored by the
152	    /// translator (`ConverseStreamOutput::ContentBlockStop(_) => {}`), included
153	    /// because a real stream closes every block it opened. Key:
154	    /// `contentBlockIndex` (`shape_content_block_stop_event.rs`).
155	    fn content_block_stop() -> Vec<u8> {
156	        frame("contentBlockStop", &json!({ "contentBlockIndex": 0 }))
157	    }
158	
159	    /// `messageStop`, the only event carrying a stop reason.
160	    ///
161	    /// `reason` is a `StopReason` wire string (`_stop_reason.rs`): `"end_turn"`
162	    /// maps to `FinishReason::Stop` and `"tool_use"` to
163	    /// `FinishReason::ToolCalls`, per `stream.rs`'s `finish_events`. Key:
164	    /// `stopReason` (`shape_message_stop_event.rs`).
165	    fn message_stop(reason: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
166	        frame(MESSAGE_STOP_EVENT_TYPE, &json!({ "stopReason": reason }))
167	    }
168	
169	    /// `metadata`, the only event carrying usage — and it arrives **after**
170	    /// `messageStop`, which is the whole reason the translator buffers the stop
171	    /// reason instead of emitting `Finish` on the spot.
172	    ///
173	    /// **This ordering is not self-enforcing, so do not reorder it casually.**
174	    /// `stream.rs` deliberately handles the reversed order too (`Metadata`
175	    /// before `MessageStop` emits `Usage` at once and `Finish` on the stop), so
176	    /// a fixture that put `metadata` first would still pass every assertion —
177	    /// while quietly testing a wire shape Bedrock does not produce, and no
178	    /// longer covering the buffering path that exists precisely because the
179	    /// real order is this one. Verified by mutation while registering this
180	    /// subject: swapping the two left the suite green.
181	    ///
182	    /// Keys: `usage` and `metrics` (`shape_converse_stream_metadata_event.rs`),
183	    /// `inputTokens` / `outputTokens` / `totalTokens` (`shape_token_usage.rs`),
184	    /// and `latencyMs` (`shape_converse_stream_metrics.rs`).
185	    fn metadata() -> Vec<u8> {
186	        frame(
187	            "metadata",
188	            &json!({
189	                "usage": { "inputTokens": 11, "outputTokens": 4, "totalTokens": 15 },
190	                "metrics": { "latencyMs": 314 }
191	            }),
192	        )
193	    }
194	
195	    /// The scripted response for one scenario, or `None` for a scenario this
196	    /// subject declines.
197	    ///
198	    /// Each script is the same Converse stream cut at a different point, so the
199	    /// scenarios differ only in what the client gets to observe — which is
200	    /// exactly the distinction the suite is checking.
201	    ///
202	    /// Returning an `Option` rather than panicking on the declined scenarios is
203	    /// what lets [`Bedrock::encodes_stop_reason`] call this for *every*
204	    /// scenario and measure the bytes.
205	    fn script(scenario: Scenario) -> Option<Script> {
206	        // The prefix every text script shares: the opening event and two
207	        // deltas, so a cancellation can be gated *between* two `TokenDelta`s
208	        // rather than before the first one.
209	        let opening = || vec![message_start(), text_delta("Hel"), text_delta("lo")];
210	        // The opening plus a completed block and a stop reason.
211	        let through_stop = || {
212	            let mut chunks = opening();
213	            chunks.push(content_block_stop());
214	            chunks.push(message_stop("end_turn"));
215	            chunks
216	        };
217	
218	        let (chunks, gate_after, ending) = match scenario {
219	            // Full stream: deltas, stop reason, then the usage-bearing metadata
220	            // event after it, then a clean end of body.
221	            Scenario::CleanStop => {
222	                let mut chunks = through_stop();
223	                chunks.push(metadata());
224	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
225	            }
226	            // The stop reason is observed, then the body simply ends — no
227	            // `metadata`, so the translator's buffered stop reason has to be
228	            // flushed by the EOF path in `model.rs` (`translator.finish()`).
229	            Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Clean),
230	            // The body ends cleanly mid-generation: no `messageStop`, so no
231	            // stop reason is ever observed and there is nothing to flush.
232	            Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Clean),
233	            // Same prefix, but the connection is torn down without the
234	            // terminating chunk, so the SDK's receiver yields a transport error.
235	            Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Abort),
236	            // The stop reason is buffered and *then* the body is aborted, so
237	            // the error path must not flush it as a `Finish`.
238	            Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Abort),
239	            // Two chunks go out — `messageStart` and the first delta — and the
240	            // server then parks, holding the second delta back. The harness
241	            // sees the stream fall quiet and cancels. No `messageStop` anywhere
242	            // in this script, so no stop reason exists even after the gate is
243	            // released.
244	            Scenario::CancelMidGeneration => (opening(), Some(2), Ending::Clean),
245	            // A whole tool call: the name arrives with the block start, the
246	            // arguments arrive split across two deltas (so exactly one emitted
247	            // `ToolCallDelta` carries the name), then a `tool_use` stop reason
248	            // and the usage-bearing metadata event.
249	            Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop => (
250	                vec![
251	                    message_start(),
252	                    tool_use_start(),
253	                    tool_use_delta("{\"city\":"),
254	                    tool_use_delta("\"Berlin\"}"),
255	                    content_block_stop(),
256	                    message_stop("tool_use"),
257	                    metadata(),
258	                ],
259	                None,
260	                Ending::Clean,
261	            ),
262	            // Declined — see the reasons in `Bedrock::stream`.
263	            Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason | Scenario::FragmentedToolName => return None,
264	            // Declined — the scenario serves an anthropic thinking block.
265	            Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => return None,
266	        };
267	
268	        Some(Script {
269	            content_type: "application/vnd.amazon.eventstream",
270	            chunks,
271	            gate_after,
272	            ending,
273	        })
274	    }

360	        fn encodes_stop_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> bool {
361	            // MEASURED from the bytes about to be served — deliberately not
362	            // `scenario.expects_stop_reason()`, which would restate the
363	            // harness's own expectation and make the cross-check dead code.
364	            //
365	            // It has to measure something, because one scenario is otherwise
366	            // undetectable if its fixture drifts: `ErrorAfterStopReason`'s
367	            // observable events are `[TokenDelta, TokenDelta, Err]`, byte-for-
368	            // byte identical to `ErrorMidGeneration`'s. If `through_stop()`
369	            // ever lost its `messageStop`, that scenario would silently degrade
370	            // into its sibling with every check in the suite still passing —
371	            // assertion 3 skips itself when an `Err` is present, and assertion 6
372	            // holds either way. This is the only guard that notices.
373	            //
374	            // A substring scan is sound here. In a `vnd.amazon.eventstream`
375	            // frame the `:event-type` header value is stored as raw ASCII, so
376	            // `"messageStop"` appears literally in any frame that carries it.
377	            // It cannot appear anywhere else in these fixtures: no other event
378	            // name this subject emits contains it (`messageStart` and
379	            // `contentBlockStop` are the near misses, and neither does), and no
380	            // payload above contains the text. `scan_finds_only_the_stop_event`
381	            // is the test that keeps that true.
382	            script(scenario)
383	                .map(|script| {
384	                    script
385	                        .chunks
386	                        .iter()
387	                        .any(|chunk| contains(chunk, MESSAGE_STOP_EVENT_TYPE.as_bytes()))
388	                })
389	                .unwrap_or(false)
390	        }

396	        fn fixture_finish_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<FinishReason> {
397	            // Exhaustive on purpose, with no `_` arm: a newly added `Scenario`
398	            // must break this match at the same time it breaks `script`'s, so
399	            // the two cannot drift. A catch-all here would silently declare
400	            // `None` for the new scenario while the build failed elsewhere.
401	            match scenario {
402	                // `"end_turn"` maps to `StopReason::EndTurn` and then to
403	                // `FinishReason::Stop` (`stream.rs`'s `finish_events`). Both of
404	                // these scenarios reach a `Finish`: `CleanStop` through the
405	                // `Metadata` path, `TruncatedAfterStopReason` through the EOF
406	                // flush.
407	                Scenario::CleanStop | Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => {
408	                    Some(FinishReason::Stop)
409	                }
410	                // `"tool_use"` maps to `StopReason::ToolUse` and then to
411	                // `FinishReason::ToolCalls`, since this request is not a
412	                // structured-output synthesis.
413	                Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop => Some(FinishReason::ToolCalls),
414	                // Truncated, errored and cancelled streams must withhold
415	                // `Finish` entirely.
416	                Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration
417	                | Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration
418	                | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
419	                | Scenario::CancelMidGeneration => None,
420	                // Declined; never reached.
421	                Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
422	                | Scenario::FragmentedToolName
423	                | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => None,
424	            }
425	        }

427	        async fn stream(&self, scenario: Scenario, cancel: CancellationToken) -> Outcome {
428	            match scenario {
429	                // The name is set once, whole, in the `contentBlockStart`
430	                // toolUse block; there is no second event it could be split
431	                // across.
432	                Scenario::FragmentedToolName => {
433	                    return Outcome::Declined("name arrives whole in toolUse start")
434	                }
435	                // The translator buffers the stop reason at `MessageStop` and
436	                // emits nothing until `Metadata`, so between "stop reason
437	                // observed" and "Finish emitted" the stream is silent. With no
438	                // event in that window there is no edge to gate on, and any
439	                // gate placed there would degrade into `CancelMidGeneration`.
440	                Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason => {
441	                    return Outcome::Declined(
442	                        "no observable event between MessageStop and Metadata",
443	                    )
444	                }
445	                Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => {
446	                    return Outcome::Declined("the scenario serves an anthropic thinking block")
447	                }
448	                _ => {}
449	            }
450	
451	            let script =
452	                script(scenario).expect("a scenario this subject serves must have a script");
453	            let mut server = PacedServer::start(script).await;
454	            let gate = server.take_gate();
455	            let model = build_model_against(&server.base_url());
456	
457	            let stream = model
458	                .invoke(request(scenario), cancel)
459	                .await
460	                .expect("bedrock invoke should reach the local paced server");
461	
462	            Outcome::Served { stream, gate }
463	        }
464	    }

467	    ///
468	    /// `[u8]` has no `contains(&[u8])`, and pulling in a dependency for one
469	    /// window scan over a fixture measured in hundreds of bytes is not worth it.
470	    fn contains(haystack: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> bool {
471	        haystack.windows(needle.len()).any(|w| w == needle)

513	/// The `Model::invoke` stream contract, checked against the OpenAI Chat
514	/// Completions backend.
515	///
516	/// This is the subject whose historical defect motivated the whole suite:
517	/// SMA-522 (PR #197), where this exact translator emitted `Finish` before
518	/// `Usage` on every streaming turn. It went undetected because the fixtures
519	/// in place at the time encoded a wire shape real OpenAI-compatible servers
520	/// do not send — `usage` arriving *before* `finish_reason` rather than after.
521	/// `CleanStop` below places `usage` after the `finish_reason` chunk for
522	/// exactly that reason.
523	///
524	/// # Fixture provenance
525	///
526	/// Every envelope shape below is transcribed from a committed fixture in this
527	/// workspace, cited on the helper that builds it:
528	///
529	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`
530	///   — the SMA-522 capture: content deltas, the `finish_reason` chunk, the
531	///   trailing `usage` chunk, `[DONE]`.
532	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/chat_wire.rs`'s
533	///   `happy_path_text_completion` fixture body — grounds the explicit
534	///   `"finish_reason":null"` OpenAI sends on every non-terminal chunk, which
535	///   is exactly the shape [`OpenAiChat::encodes_stop_reason`]'s marker must
536	///   not match.
537	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt`
538	///   — the tool-call envelope: `id`/`name` arriving with empty `arguments`,
539	///   followed by args-only continuations with no `name` key.
540	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/fixtures/tool_call_stream_fragmented_name.txt`
541	///   — the committed capture of a name split across two deltas that BOTH
542	///   arrive after the `id`. Per the design spec's §6 provenance note, this is
543	///   the capture `FragmentedToolName`'s shape must be drawn from — the note
544	///   requires the committed **shape**, not byte-identical values; see
545	///   "`FragmentedToolName` deliberately never completes" below for exactly
546	///   what this module substitutes (the "id resolves late" variant has no
547	///   capture anywhere in the repo and is not built here).
548	///
549	/// `chat_content_filter.txt` and `chat_text_usage_trailing_empty_choices.txt`
550	/// were read but contribute no shape this module needs: this subject serves
551	/// only `Stop` and `ToolCalls` finish reasons, and the empty-`choices` usage
552	/// variant is a second encoding of the same trailing-usage envelope already
553	/// covered by `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`.
554	///
555	/// # `FragmentedToolName` deliberately never completes
556	///
557	/// The task brief's scenario table describes `FragmentedToolName` as ending
558	/// with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` → `usage` → `[DONE]`, mirroring the
559	/// litellm capture's full trace. That shape was tried first and reverted: the
560	/// design spec's §6 table asserts only **7, 1** for this scenario (`S6`), not
561	/// 3/4, and `Scenario::expects_stop_reason` (`src/lib.rs`) excludes
562	/// `FragmentedToolName` from the set of scenarios that may observe a stop
563	/// reason. Completing the stream — which the real translator does, buffering
564	/// `finish_reason` and flushing it as a genuine `Finish` at end-of-stream —
565	/// makes `encodes_stop_reason` measure `true` against an `expects_stop_reason`
566	/// of `false`, failing on `StopReasonDeclarationMismatch` before the stream is
567	/// even drained. So this subject's `FragmentedToolName` script draws its
568	/// event sequence and key structure from that capture's first three frames —
569	/// not a byte-identical copy: `id`/`created`/`model` are this module's fixed
570	/// constants (`RESPONSE_ID`/`MODEL_ID`) rather than the capture's literal
571	/// values, `TOOL_CALL_ID` stands in for the capture's literal tool-call id,
572	/// and the first frame omits the capture's `"role":"assistant"` key
573	/// (`ChatTranslator` does not read it) — see the `FragmentedToolName` match
574	/// arm in `script`, below, for the exact substitutions. The body ends
575	/// cleanly right after those three frames — no `finish_reason`, no `usage`,
576	/// no `[DONE]`. Assertion 7 (exactly one name-bearing delta per `call_id`) is
577	/// fully exercised by that prefix alone; nothing here shortens what the
578	/// scenario tests, only when its script stops.
579	///
580	/// # SMA-566's alias regression coverage lives in the crate's own unit tests
581	///
582	/// Every tool-call delta this module scripts carries an explicit `"index":0`,
583	/// and no delta ever introduces a second `id` — the continuation frames
584	/// (`tool_call_name_fragment`, `tool_call_args`) omit the key entirely. Only
585	/// one index value is ever in play, so the two-index-one-id shape that
586	/// `ChatTranslator::canonicalize` exists to merge never arises from these
587	/// bytes, and assertion 7 passes here without exercising it. Under
588	/// this suite's fixture-provenance rule the shape has no capture anywhere in
589	/// the repo and must not be invented, so it is not registered as a scenario —
590	/// exactly as `litellm` records for its own `canonicalize`.
591	///
592	/// Read this subject's `conforms` test as confirming the translator behaves
593	/// correctly on the wire shapes OpenAI is actually observed to send, **not**
594	/// as a standing regression guard for the alias fix. That guard is
595	/// `two_indexes_with_one_id_merge_into_a_single_call` and its eleven siblings
596	/// in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs`. If a
597	/// future capture ever shows a backend reusing one `id` across two indexes,
598	/// that would be the fixture to add here; none currently committed does.

600	    use super::*;

600	    use super::*;
601	    use paigasus_helikon_providers_openai::OpenAiModel;

603	    /// `id` on every scripted chunk. Not claimed to match any real OpenAI id
604	    /// format — nothing under test inspects it — fixed purely so failure

606	    const RESPONSE_ID: &str = "chatcmpl-conformance";
607	
608	    /// `model` on every scripted chunk, and the model id `build_model_against`
609	    /// requests. Matches the identifier the task brief specifies.
610	    const MODEL_ID: &str = "gpt-4o-mini";
611	
612	    /// The tool name every tool-call fixture declares.
613	    const TOOL_NAME: &str = "get_weather";
614	
615	    /// `id` for the single tool call in the tool fixtures. Fixed for the same
616	    /// reason as [`RESPONSE_ID`].
617	    const TOOL_CALL_ID: &str = "call_conformance_0";
618	
619	    /// The substring that appears in a Chat Completions chunk if and only if
620	    /// that chunk carries a *populated* `finish_reason`.
621	    ///
622	    /// The obvious marker — `finish_reason` alone — is wrong for this
623	    /// subject: OpenAI sends `"finish_reason":null` on every ordinary content
624	    /// or tool-call delta (see [`text_delta`]), so a bare substring scan would
625	    /// report a stop reason for scripts that encode none. Scanning for the
626	    /// opening quote of a *string* value excludes the null case: `null` has
627	    /// no quote after the colon, `"stop"`/`"tool_calls"` do.
628	    /// `scan_finds_only_a_populated_finish_reason` is the guard that keeps
629	    /// this true as helpers are added or edited.
630	    const FINISH_REASON_MARKER: &[u8] = b"\"finish_reason\":\"";
631	
632	    /// One SSE frame: `data: {payload}\n\n`. `serde_json::Value`'s `Display`
633	    /// impl serialises compactly (no extra whitespace), which is what keeps
634	    /// [`FINISH_REASON_MARKER`] a literal substring of the bytes on the wire.
635	    fn frame(payload: serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8> {
636	        format!("data: {payload}\n\n").into_bytes()
637	    }

639	    /// One text delta.
640	    ///
641	    /// Envelope shape (`id`/`object`/`created`/`model`/`choices[].index`/
642	    /// `choices[].delta.content`) matches the content-delta chunks in
643	    /// `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`. The explicit `"finish_reason":null` is
644	    /// grounded in `tests/chat_wire.rs`'s `happy_path_text_completion`

646	    /// `scan_finds_only_a_populated_finish_reason` uses to prove the marker
647	    /// does not fire on a null value.
648	    fn text_delta(text: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
649	        frame(json!({
650	            "id": RESPONSE_ID,
651	            "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
652	            "created": 1,
653	            "model": MODEL_ID,
654	            "choices": [{
655	                "index": 0,
656	                "delta": { "content": text },
657	                "finish_reason": null
658	            }]
659	        }))
660	    }
661	
662	    /// The chunk carrying a populated `finish_reason`. Matches
663	    /// `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`'s finish chunk
664	    /// (`"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"`).
665	    ///
666	    /// `ChatTranslator` buffers this and does **not** emit `Finish` inline —
667	    /// it is released only by `finish()` at end-of-stream
668	    /// (`backend/chat.rs`'s `consume`/`finish` doc comments) — which is the
669	    /// whole reason `CleanStop` must place [`usage_chunk`] *after* this one:
670	    /// that ordering is the exact shape SMA-522 got wrong.
671	    fn finish_chunk(reason: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
672	        frame(json!({
673	            "id": RESPONSE_ID,
674	            "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
675	            "created": 1,
676	            "model": MODEL_ID,
677	            "choices": [{ "index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": reason }]
678	        }))
679	    }
680	
681	    /// The trailing usage-only chunk. Matches `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`'s
682	    /// usage chunk's shape: an empty `delta`, no `finish_reason` key at all,
683	    /// and a top-level `usage` object.
684	    fn usage_chunk() -> Vec<u8> {
685	        frame(json!({
686	            "id": RESPONSE_ID,
687	            "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
688	            "created": 1,
689	            "model": MODEL_ID,
690	            "choices": [{ "index": 0, "delta": {} }],
691	            "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 8, "completion_tokens": 6, "total_tokens": 14 }
692	        }))
693	    }

696	    /// `async-openai`'s `create_stream` consumes `[DONE]` internally and ends
697	    /// iteration on it (`backend/chat.rs`'s `invoke` doc comment), so it never
698	    /// reaches the translator as an event — it only has to be present for a
699	    /// script to be the stream it claims to be.
700	    fn done() -> Vec<u8> {
701	        b"data: [DONE]\n\n".to_vec()
702	    }

704	    /// `id` plus a name fragment, empty `arguments`. Matches

773	    /// The scripted response for one scenario.
774	    ///
775	    /// Returns `None` for `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop`, which this subject
776	    /// declines, like `bedrock::script`.
777	    fn script(scenario: Scenario) -> Option<Script> {
778	        // The two-delta opening every text scenario shares. The content is
779	        // arbitrary (as in `bedrock::opening`); the envelope is what is
780	        // grounded — see `text_delta`.
781	        let opening = || vec![text_delta("Hel"), text_delta("lo")];
782	        // The opening plus a populated finish_reason chunk.
783	        let through_stop = || {
784	            let mut chunks = opening();
785	            chunks.push(finish_chunk("stop"));
786	            chunks
787	        };
788	
789	        let (chunks, gate_after, ending) = match scenario {
790	            // Full stream: deltas, stop reason, then usage AFTER it, then
791	            // [DONE] and a clean end of body. Usage-after-finish_reason is
792	            // the real OpenAI wire order and the exact shape SMA-522 got
793	            // wrong — see the module doc.
794	            Scenario::CleanStop => {
795	                let mut chunks = through_stop();
796	                chunks.push(usage_chunk());
797	                chunks.push(done());
798	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
799	            }
800	            // The stop reason is observed, then the body simply ends — no
801	            // usage, no [DONE] — so the translator's buffered stop reason has
802	            // to be flushed by the EOF path (`ChatTranslator::finish`).
803	            Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Clean),
804	            // The body ends cleanly mid-generation: no finish_reason chunk
805	            // ever arrives, so no stop reason is ever observed.
806	            Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Clean),
807	            // Same prefix, but the connection is torn down without a
808	            // terminating chunk, so the client observes a transport error.
809	            Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Abort),
810	            // The stop reason is buffered and *then* the body is aborted, so
811	            // the error path must not flush it as a Finish.
812	            Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Abort),
813	            // One content delta goes out, then the server parks holding the
814	            // second back (`gate_after: Some(1)` pauses *before* sending the
815	            // chunk at index 1, per `server.rs`'s `feed` loop) — no
816	            // finish_reason chunk anywhere in this script, so no stop reason
817	            // exists even after the gate releases.
818	            Scenario::CancelMidGeneration => {
819	                let chunks = opening();
820	                (chunks, Some(1), Ending::Clean)
821	            }
822	            // The stop reason AND the usage chunk after it are both observed
823	            // before the gate. `usage` is the harness's required edge here:
824	            // `ChatTranslator` buffers `finish_reason` silently
825	            // (`backend/chat.rs`'s `consume` doc comment), so the stop-reason
826	            // chunk itself is not an observable event — usage is the first
827	            // thing the client sees after it, and the floor in
828	            // `assert_conforms` requires at least one `Usage` for this exact
829	            // reason (see its `CancelAfterStopReason` comment).
830	            Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason => {
831	                let mut chunks = through_stop();
832	                chunks.push(usage_chunk());
833	                let gate_after = chunks.len();
834	                (chunks, Some(gate_after), Ending::Clean)
835	            }
836	            // The committed capture's event sequence and key structure for
837	            // its first three frames, not a byte-identical copy: `id`/
838	            // `created`/`model` are this module's fixed constants
839	            // (`RESPONSE_ID`/`MODEL_ID`) rather than the capture's
840	            // `"chatcmpl-fake"`/`1786999074`/`"shape-fragment"` values,
841	            // `TOOL_CALL_ID` stands in for the capture's literal
842	            // `"call_abc"`, and [`tool_call_start`]'s frame omits the
843	            // capture's `"role":"assistant"` key — `ChatTranslator` does not
844	            // read it, the same reason every other omitted-but-unread field
845	            // in this module is dropped. See the module doc's
846	            // "FragmentedToolName deliberately never completes" section for
847	            // why the body ends right here rather than continuing on to the
848	            // capture's finish_reason/usage/[DONE] tail.
849	            Scenario::FragmentedToolName => {
850	                let chunks = vec![
851	                    tool_call_start(TOOL_CALL_ID, "get_"),
852	                    tool_call_name_fragment("weather"),
853	                    tool_call_args("{\"city\":\"Berlin\"}"),
854	                ];
855	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
856	            }
857	            // A whole tool call: the name arrives with the first delta
858	            // (empty args), the arguments arrive on the next delta (so
859	            // exactly one emitted `ToolCallDelta` carries the name), then a
860	            // tool_calls stop reason and the usage-bearing trailing chunk.
861	            Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop => {
862	                let chunks = vec![
863	                    tool_call_start(TOOL_CALL_ID, TOOL_NAME),
864	                    tool_call_args("{\"city\":\"Berlin\"}"),
865	                    finish_chunk("tool_calls"),
866	                    usage_chunk(),
867	                    done(),
868	                ];
869	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
870	            }
871	            // Declined — the scenario serves an anthropic thinking block.
872	            Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => return None,
873	        };
874	
875	        Some(Script {
876	            content_type: "text/event-stream",
877	            chunks,
878	            gate_after,
879	            ending,
880	        })
881	    }

1040	/// The `Model::invoke` stream contract, checked against the LiteLLM proxy's
1041	/// Chat Completions backend.
1042	///
1043	/// LiteLLM's wire shape is the OpenAI Chat Completions envelope
1044	/// (`openai_chat` above is its closest sibling in this suite), but SMA-550
1045	/// fixed a real correlation bug in this translator specifically:
1046	/// `providers-litellm/src/stream.rs` used to key buffered tool-call fragments
1047	/// by their *wire* key (`Index`/`Id`) rather than canonicalizing on the
1048	/// resolved `call_id`, so one call could own two state entries and emit two
1049	/// name-bearing deltas. Since the fix, every delta for one call is
1050	/// re-keyed onto a single canonical `Key::Id(call_id)` slot
1051	/// (`ChatTranslator::canonicalize`), which is what makes assertion 7 —
1052	/// "exactly one name-carrying `ToolCallDelta` per `call_id`" — structural
1053	/// for the translator in general. **It is not, however, probed by this
1054	/// module's own fixtures** — see the section below on where that coverage
1055	/// actually lives.
1056	///
1057	/// # Fixture provenance
1058	///
1059	/// Every envelope shape below is transcribed from a fixture committed in
1060	/// `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/fixtures/`, cited on the
1061	/// helper that builds it:
1062	///
1063	/// - `text_then_trailing_usage.txt` — content deltas with no `finish_reason`
1064	///   key at all (not even an explicit `null`), a chunk carrying a populated
1065	///   `finish_reason`, a trailing usage-only chunk with no `finish_reason` key,
1066	///   `[DONE]`.
1067	/// - `tool_call_stream.txt` — the whole-tool-call envelope: `id` and the
1068	///   complete function `name` arriving together with an empty-string
1069	///   `arguments`, followed by two args-only continuations with no `name` key
1070	///   at all (not even empty), then a `"tool_calls"` finish chunk and trailing
1071	///   usage.
1072	/// - `tool_call_stream_fragmented_name.txt` — captured against LiteLLM
1073	///   1.98.0; the canonical fragmented-name shape, both fragments arriving
1074	///   after the id (the first fragment arrives together with the id, the
1075	///   second on a later delta once the id has already resolved). Per the
1076	///   design spec's §6 provenance note the "id resolves late" variant has no
1077	///   capture anywhere in the repo and is not built here — matching
1078	///   `openai_chat`'s note on the same file.
1079	/// - `truncated_no_finish.txt` — grounds the shape "content delta(s), then
1080	///   the body simply ends" with no `finish_reason` chunk anywhere.
1081	///
1082	/// `unknown_finish_reason.txt` was read but contributes no shape this module
1083	/// needs: this subject serves only `Stop` and `ToolCalls` finish reasons, and
1084	/// the `"guardrail_intervened"` shape it captures is a second encoding of the
1085	/// already-covered populated-`finish_reason` envelope.
1086	///
1087	/// [`FINISH_REASON_MARKER`]'s guard test needs one more shape that no
1088	/// committed *litellm-crate* fixture happens to carry: a content delta with
1089	/// an **explicit** `"finish_reason":null`. That shape is grounded exactly as
1090	/// `openai_chat` grounds it — via
1091	/// `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/chat_wire.rs`'s
1092	/// `happy_path_text_completion` fixture body, whose own comment records it as
1093	/// "Captured from LiteLLM". This module's own `text_delta` stays faithful to
1094	/// `text_then_trailing_usage.txt` (which omits the key rather than nulling
1095	/// it), so that second shape is scripted only inside the guard test, not
1096	/// served to the subject.
1097	///
1098	/// # `FragmentedToolName` draws its shape, not its literal values, from the
1099	/// capture
1100	///
1101	/// Per `Scenario::expects_stop_reason` (`src/lib.rs`) and the design spec's
1102	/// §6 table (`7, 1` only, no assertion 3), this scenario must not carry a
1103	/// `finish_reason`. `tool_call_stream_fragmented_name.txt`'s capture
1104	/// continues on to a `"tool_calls"` finish chunk and trailing usage, but this
1105	/// subject's script stops right after the three tool-call deltas — see
1106	/// `openai_chat`'s module doc for the full reasoning (same shape, same fix,
1107	/// same file). As in every other scenario in this module, `id`/`created`/
1108	/// `model` are this module's fixed constants rather than the capture's
1109	/// literal values, and `TOOL_CALL_ID` stands in for the capture's literal
1110	/// tool-call id; unlike `openai_chat`'s version of this same scenario,
1111	/// this module's `tool_call_start` keeps the capture's `"role":"assistant"`
1112	/// key.
1113	///
1114	/// # `canonicalize`'s SMA-550 regression coverage lives in the crate's own
1115	/// unit tests, not here
1116	///
1117	/// Both `tool_call_stream.txt` and `tool_call_stream_fragmented_name.txt`
1118	/// carry an explicit `"index":0` on *every* tool-call delta. Because of
1119	/// that, `handle_tool_call` (`stream.rs:373-448`) already resolves every
1120	/// delta for one call to the same `call_id` via
1121	/// `self.tool_calls.get(&Key::Index(0))` alone — the `Key::Index`/`Key::Id`
1122	/// boundary that `ChatTranslator::canonicalize` exists to unify never arises
1123	/// from these specific bytes.
1124	///
1125	/// Confirmed by mutation while registering this subject: temporarily
1126	/// stubbing `canonicalize` into an identity function left `litellm::conforms`
1127	/// green, while the same change failed **11 tests** in
1128	/// `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/stream.rs`'s own test
1129	/// module — most directly
1130	/// `stream::tests::dual_key_call_emits_at_most_one_name_mid_stream`, which
1131	/// observes exactly the pre-SMA-550 shape (two name-carrying deltas for one
1132	/// `call_id`) that neither of this subject's tool scenarios can reproduce.
1133	///
1134	/// So: read this subject's `conforms` test as confirming the translator
1135	/// behaves correctly on the wire shapes LiteLLM is actually observed to
1136	/// send, **not** as a standing regression guard for the `canonicalize` fix
1137	/// itself — that guard is `dual_key_call_emits_at_most_one_name_mid_stream`
1138	/// and its ten siblings, in the crate under test. If a future litellm
1139	/// capture ever shows a backend whose `index`/`id` correlation key changes
1140	/// mid-call, that would be the fixture to add here; none currently
1141	/// committed does.
1142	mod litellm {
1143	    use super::*;
1144	    use paigasus_helikon_providers_litellm::LiteLlmModel;
1145	
1146	    /// `id` on every scripted chunk. Not claimed to match any real LiteLLM id
1147	    /// format — nothing under test inspects it — fixed purely so failure
1148	    /// output is stable and greppable.
1149	    const RESPONSE_ID: &str = "chatcmpl-conformance";
1150	
1151	    /// `model` on every scripted chunk, and the model alias `build_model_against`
1152	    /// requests. Matches the alias the task brief specifies.
1153	    const MODEL_ID: &str = "prod-fast";

1157	
1158	    /// `id` for the single tool call in the tool fixtures. Fixed for the same
1159	    /// reason as [`RESPONSE_ID`].

1160	    const TOOL_CALL_ID: &str = "call_conformance_0";
1161	
1162	    /// The substring that appears in a chunk if and only if it carries a
1163	    /// *populated* `finish_reason`.
1164	    ///
1165	    /// The obvious marker — `finish_reason` alone — would be wrong even
1166	    /// though this subject's own `text_delta` chunks omit the key entirely
1167	    /// (see [`text_delta`]): OpenAI-compatible backends behind LiteLLM can
1168	    /// still emit an explicit `"finish_reason":null` on an ordinary delta, so
1169	    /// the marker has to exclude that shape structurally, not merely happen
1170	    /// to avoid the one shape this module scripts. Scanning for the opening
1171	    /// quote of a *string* value does that: `null` has no quote after the
1172	    /// colon, `"stop"`/`"tool_calls"` do.
1173	    /// `scan_finds_only_a_populated_finish_reason` is the guard that keeps
1174	    /// this true, including against a literal `"finish_reason":null` chunk.
1175	    const FINISH_REASON_MARKER: &[u8] = b"\"finish_reason\":\"";
1176	
1177	    /// One SSE frame: `data: {payload}\n\n`. `serde_json::Value`'s `Display`
1178	    /// impl serialises compactly (no extra whitespace), which is what keeps
1179	    /// [`FINISH_REASON_MARKER`] a literal substring of the bytes on the wire.
1180	    fn frame(payload: serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8> {
1181	        format!("data: {payload}\n\n").into_bytes()
1182	    }

1184	    /// One text delta. Matches `text_then_trailing_usage.txt`'s content
1185	    /// chunks: no `finish_reason` key at all, not even `null`.
1186	    fn text_delta(text: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
1187	        frame(json!({
1188	            "id": RESPONSE_ID,
1189	            "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
1190	            "created": 1,
1191	            "model": MODEL_ID,
1192	            "choices": [{
1193	                "index": 0,
1194	                "delta": { "content": text }
1195	            }]
1196	        }))
1197	    }
1198	
1199	    /// The chunk carrying a populated `finish_reason`. Matches
1200	    /// `text_then_trailing_usage.txt`'s finish chunk
1201	    /// (`"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"`).
1202	    ///
1203	    /// `ChatTranslator` buffers this and does **not** emit `Finish` inline —
1204	    /// it is released only by `finish()` at end-of-stream (`stream.rs`'s
1205	    /// module doc, invariant 1) — which is why `CleanStop` below must place
1206	    /// [`usage_chunk`] *after* this one.
1207	    fn finish_chunk(reason: &str) -> Vec<u8> {

1308	    /// The scripted response for one scenario.
1309	    ///
1310	    /// Returns `None` for `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop`, which this subject
1311	    /// declines.
1312	    fn script(scenario: Scenario) -> Option<Script> {
1313	        // The two-delta opening every text scenario shares, matching
1314	        // `text_then_trailing_usage.txt`'s two content chunks.
1315	        let opening = || vec![text_delta("Hel"), text_delta("lo")];
1316	        // The opening plus a populated finish_reason chunk.
1317	        let through_stop = || {
1318	            let mut chunks = opening();
1319	            chunks.push(finish_chunk("stop"));
1320	            chunks
1321	        };
1322	
1323	        let (chunks, gate_after, ending) = match scenario {
1324	            // Full stream: deltas, stop reason, then usage AFTER it, then
1325	            // [DONE] and a clean end of body — the exact order
1326	            // `text_then_trailing_usage.txt` captures.
1327	            Scenario::CleanStop => {
1328	                let mut chunks = through_stop();
1329	                chunks.push(usage_chunk());
1330	                chunks.push(done());
1331	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
1332	            }
1333	            // The stop reason is observed, then the body simply ends — no
1334	            // usage, no [DONE] — so the translator's buffered stop reason has
1335	            // to be flushed by the EOF path (`ChatTranslator::finish`).
1336	            Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Clean),
1337	            // The body ends cleanly mid-generation: no finish_reason chunk
1338	            // ever arrives, so no stop reason is ever observed. Grounded in
1339	            // `truncated_no_finish.txt`'s shape (content delta(s), then EOF).
1340	            Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Clean),
1341	            // Same prefix, but the connection is torn down without a
1342	            // terminating chunk, so the client observes a transport error.
1343	            Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration => (opening(), None, Ending::Abort),
1344	            // The stop reason is buffered and *then* the body is aborted, so
1345	            // the error path must not flush it as a Finish. This is the one
1346	            // scenario byte-identical to ErrorMidGeneration's observable
1347	            // events, which is exactly what `encodes_stop_reason` exists to
1348	            // keep distinguishable — see its doc.
1349	            Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Abort),
1350	            // One content delta goes out, then the server parks holding the
1351	            // second back (`gate_after: Some(1)` pauses *before* sending the
1352	            // chunk at index 1, per `server.rs`'s `feed` loop) — no
1353	            // finish_reason chunk anywhere in this script, so no stop reason
1354	            // exists even after the gate releases.
1355	            Scenario::CancelMidGeneration => {
1356	                let chunks = opening();
1357	                (chunks, Some(1), Ending::Clean)
1358	            }
1359	            // The stop reason AND the usage chunk after it are both observed
1360	            // before the gate. `usage` is the harness's required edge here:
1361	            // `ChatTranslator` buffers `finish_reason` silently, so the
1362	            // stop-reason chunk itself is not an observable event — usage is
1363	            // the first thing the client sees after it.
1364	            Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason => {
1365	                let mut chunks = through_stop();
1366	                chunks.push(usage_chunk());
1367	                let gate_after = chunks.len();
1368	                (chunks, Some(gate_after), Ending::Clean)
1369	            }
1370	            // `tool_call_stream_fragmented_name.txt`'s event sequence and key
1371	            // structure for its first three frames, not a byte-identical
1372	            // copy (see the module doc's "`FragmentedToolName` draws its
1373	            // shape, not its literal values, from the capture" section for
1374	            // the substitutions) — and nothing more: no finish_reason, no
1375	            // usage, no [DONE]. See that same section for why the body ends
1376	            // right here.
1377	            Scenario::FragmentedToolName => {
1378	                let chunks = vec![
1379	                    tool_call_start(TOOL_CALL_ID, "get_"),
1380	                    tool_call_name_fragment("weather"),
1381	                    tool_call_args("{\"city\":\"Berlin\"}"),
1382	                ];
1383	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
1384	            }
1385	            // `tool_call_stream.txt`'s event sequence and key structure, not
1386	            // its literal values: `id`/`created`/`model` are this module's
1387	            // fixed constants (`RESPONSE_ID`/`MODEL_ID`) rather than the
1388	            // capture's `"chatcmpl-fake"`/`1786999072`/`"shape-normal"`, and
1389	            // `TOOL_CALL_ID` stands in for the capture's literal
1390	            // `"call_abc"` (same substitution convention as every other
1391	            // scenario in this module). What the fixture actually grounds:
1392	            // the whole name arrives with the id (empty args), the arguments
1393	            // arrive split across two continuations (so exactly one emitted
1394	            // `ToolCallDelta` carries the name), then a tool_calls stop
1395	            // reason and the usage-bearing trailing chunk.
1396	            Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop => {
1397	                let chunks = vec![
1398	                    tool_call_start(TOOL_CALL_ID, TOOL_NAME),
1399	                    tool_call_args("{\"city\":"),
1400	                    tool_call_args("\"Berlin\"}"),
1401	                    finish_chunk("tool_calls"),
1402	                    usage_chunk(),
1403	                    done(),
1404	                ];
1405	                (chunks, None, Ending::Clean)
1406	            }
1407	            // Declined — the scenario serves an anthropic thinking block.
1408	            Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => return None,
1409	        };
1410	
1411	        Some(Script {
1412	            content_type: "text/event-stream",
1413	            chunks,
1414	            gate_after,
1415	            ending,
1416	        })
1417	    }

1668	/// # Why `Ending::Abort` and not the fixtures' own `error` event

1685	/// way across every subject, rather than re-deriving Anthropic's in-band error

1687	/// mechanisms are indistinguishable to this driver either way: `model.rs`'s

1692	/// # Three things specific to this provider

: that a no-argument tool would stream zero `function_call_arguments.delta`
: frames, leaving `Finish{ToolCalls}` with no `ToolCallDelta` to match it. It
: does not: the API streams exactly one delta carrying the literal `{}`. The
: same shape was confirmed on gpt-5-mini. The zero-delta stream SMA-562 fixes
: is real, but it comes from resuming a stored background response past its
: deltas -- which has no `output_item.added` either, so it cannot be served
: from this directory's POST-only wiremock harness and is driven as typed
: events in `backend/responses.rs`'s test module instead.

: the translator already had, so that if OpenAI ever elides the `{}` delta the
: assumption is at least written down. Note what a frozen fixture cannot do:
: notice that change happening.

: CORRECTION (final review, post-implementation): this header used to claim

: assertion that can [notice], and is the reason it exists." That is no

: `response.completed` sweep, that synthesises a ToolCallDelta from the
: terminal item for any call that streamed no argument deltas at all (the

42	//! ```
43	//!
44	//! ## Structured output
45	//!
46	//! Set `ModelSettings::response_format` to `ResponseFormat::JsonSchema`. The
47	//! provider passes the schema directly to Gemini's `generationConfig.responseSchema`
48	//! field (native structured output — no forced-tool synthesis). A JSON-Schema
49	//! sanitizer runs automatically to strip unsupported keywords and rewrite
50	//! incompatible constructs before sending.
51	//!
52	//! Note: Gemini rejects requests that combine `responseSchema` with active
53	//! function calling. The provider returns a conflict error before sending if
54	//! the request has non-empty tools OR a tool choice other than `None`.
55	//!
56	//! ## Limitations
57	//!
58	//! Remote-URL images, audio parts, and non-text tool-result parts are silently
59	//! dropped during request translation. Reasoning streaming (`ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta`)
60	//! is not yet emitted by this provider.
61	//!
62	//! Tool loops work with thought signatures. The provider keeps each signature
63	//! and sends it back on its own call. When no call in a model content of the
64	//! current turn has a valid signature, it puts the documented dummy value on
65	//! each call of that content. The dummy is live-tested only on
66	//! `gemini-3.8-flash` (Developer API). Vertex signatures are not live-tested.
67	//! Text-level signatures are not sent back.
68	//!
69	//! A request that ends with a model turn gets a `user` text turn "Continue."
70	//! appended, because Gemini rejects such a request.
71	//!
72	//! Gemini 1.x and 2.x models are not supported. A model id that the crate does
73	//! not know reports a conservative capability set (streaming and tools). Use
74	//! `.with_capabilities()` on the builder to set other values.
75	
76	/// Key under which this crate stores its data in `ProviderData` parts and events.
77	pub const PROVIDER_DATA_KEY: &str = "gemini";

use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::Value;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]

pub(crate) struct GeminiChunk {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) candidates: Vec<Candidate>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) usage_metadata: Option<UsageMetadata>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) prompt_feedback: Option<PromptFeedback>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub(crate) struct Candidate {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) content: Option<Content>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) finish_reason: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct Content {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) parts: Vec<Part>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub(crate) struct Part {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) text: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) function_call: Option<FunctionCall>,
    /// Kept as raw JSON, so a value that is not a string never rejects the
    /// chunk. The translator reads only a string.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) thought_signature: Option<Value>,

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct FunctionCall {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) id: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) args: Value,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub(crate) struct UsageMetadata {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) prompt_token_count: u32,

    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) cached_content_token_count: Option<u32>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) thoughts_token_count: Option<u32>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub(crate) struct PromptFeedback {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub(crate) block_reason: Option<String>,
}

The core work and the work in other crates do not depend on the wire shape, so they can start
before the probe results. The Gemini stream and request work waits for the results. If capture 1
shows a different wire shape than this design expects, stop and bring it to Sven. Fixtures are
transcribed from the captures, with each real signature replaced by a placeholder. No real
signature goes into the repo or the PR body. Vertex is not probed; the spec states this limit in the
Gemini README.

### Probe results (2026-11-20)

Sven ran the probe against the Developer API on `gemini-3.8-flash`. No real signature value is
recorded here. Lengths are given.

**Capture 1 (streamed, three parallel calls).** HTTP 200, `finishReason` STOP. The stream has four
SSE chunks. Chunks 0 to 2 each hold one part with one `functionCall`. Chunk 3 holds `{"text": ""}`
with `finishReason: STOP` and no signature. `functionCall.id` is present on every call (native ids
of the form `call_<digits>`). `thoughtSignature` is a sibling of `functionCall` in the same part and
the same chunk. It is on the first call only, and it is 1140 characters long. The other two calls
have no signature. This matches the design.

Core sorts calls by `call_id` (`BTreeMap`). In this capture the sort moved the signed call from
first to last. So the order risk is real, and the `index` field is needed to restore the order.

**Capture 2 (streamed text answer).** Four text chunks. The last chunk is
`{"text": "", "thoughtSignature": <3036 characters>}`. A text-level signature exists, on an empty
final text part. The design ignores it (non-goal).

**Second turns (`generateContent`).**

| Capture | Shape | HTTP | finish | promptTokenCount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | real signature as received | 200 | STOP | 351 |
| 4 | signed call moved to last | 200 | STOP | 351 |
| 5 | signed first, two unsigned calls swapped | 200 | STOP | 351 |
| 6 | dummy on each call | 200 | STOP | 183 |
| 7 | no signature | 400 "Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts", position 2 | - | - |
| 8 | SMA-820 shape 3, merged `user[functionResponse x3, text]`, real signature | 200 | STOP | 357 |
| 9 | other model | skipped (`GEMINI_MODEL_ID_2` not set) | - | - |

**Conclusions.**

- The wire shape matches the design. No stop condition triggers on capture 1 or 3.
- Gemini does not check the order of the calls (captures 4 and 5). The `index` sort is not required.
  The design keeps it, because it is harmless and it restores what Gemini sent.
- The signature is billed input: 351 against 183 prompt tokens for one 1140-character signature,
  about 168 tokens. This triggered the plan's stop condition. Sven decided that the core token
  estimate counts `ProviderData` as the serialized length of `data`, not 0.
- The merged shape (capture 8) gets HTTP 200 with the real signature. So the SMA-820 tool-result
  boundary is not needed when signatures are present. See "Left for Sven".
