## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK
Most of the mechanics are sound: assertions 9 and 10, the two new scenarios, and the UNCAPTURED table. But three central claims are false when checked against the code: the G1 contract sentence conflicts with Bedrock, the anthropic thinking script has no text block, and the four UNCAPTURED thinking rows cannot be closed by a capture. §5 (D4, D5), §6.6 and §6.7 need rework, and one item needs a decision from Sven before implementation.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **The G1 contract sentence makes Bedrock non-conformant** - §3.3 checks only LiteLLM. The Bedrock SMA-833 path pushes an `Err`, then emits `Usage` when `metadata` arrives (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:150-160). The test `forbid_tool_calls_turns_a_tool_use_into_an_error` (same file, :848-869) asserts that `out[1]` is a `Usage` after the `Err`. The Bedrock driver yields every item from `consume` and does not return after an inner `Err` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/model.rs:173-177). The Anthropic driver also continues after an inner `Err`, for example a `refusal` at `message_stop` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/model.rs:150-154, stream.rs:383). The gemini, openai and litellm drivers return after an `Err`. No conformance scenario serves these paths, so assertion 9 stays green. | Why it matters: the PR would add a MUST to core that a published crate breaks, and a test in that crate pins the breach. §7 says that a defect that needs a design decision stops the work. | Suggested fix: decide before implementation. Option A: the Bedrock and Anthropic drivers return after they yield an inner `Err`, and the Bedrock test changes, so the `Usage` after the error is lost. Option B: the sentence allows `Usage` after `Err`, and assertion 9 exempts it. In both cases, add a translator-level test, because the suite cannot reach this path.

- **The anthropic thinking script has no text block, so the declared order `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]` fails** - The served `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop` script removes the text block of the capture (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs:2092-2119; the comment at 2097-2100 says so). With the current translator, the observed runs are `[Reasoning, Tool]`. So the D4 statement "the suite already serves exactly that capture" is false. §6.8 gives the conforming fake `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]`, so the unit tests stay green and do not show the mismatch. | Why it matters: as written, anthropic fails with `ChannelOrderMismatch` on the first run. Or the builder changes the declaration to `[Reasoning, Tool]`, which cannot show that text stays between reasoning and the tool call. That is the main property that G2 can test. | Suggested fix: tell the builder to restore the text block from `thinking_text_tool_use.txt` (text at index 1, `tool_use` at index 2), to update the provenance comment, and to declare `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]`. The text block then emits a Text-position `ProviderData` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:275-279). Assertion 8 still passes, because that event has no `call_id`. A better fix: measure the channel order from the script bytes, as `encodes_stop_reason` does, so that this drift fails automatically.

- **The four UNCAPTURED rows for `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop` are false, and D5 contradicts itself** - The scenario floor requires a call-scoped `ProviderData` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/lib.rs:574-588). After this change, it also requires at least one `ReasoningDelta`. Only the anthropic and gemini streams emit `ProviderData`. The bedrock, litellm and openai/responses stream translators emit none. Gemini emits no `ReasoningDelta` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/lib.rs:59-60). Its request never sets `includeThoughts` or `thinkingConfig`, so no thought part comes on the wire. A capture alone cannot let any of the four subjects serve this scenario. Also, the new openai/chat reason "the chat translator reads no reasoning field" is about the translator, which D5 itself forbids. The same reason applies to gemini, but gemini goes to UNCAPTURED. | Why it matters: the pinned table would say "only a capture is missing" when that is not true, and the follow-up issue cannot be closed as written. The anti-goals forbid this kind of false table row. | Suggested fix: reverse D4. Keep `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop` as the anthropic signed-thinking scenario. Rewrite its DECLINED reasons as true statements, for example "the stream emits no call-scoped ProviderData for a thinking block". Add a provider-neutral `ReasoningCleanStop` with three floors: at least one `ReasoningDelta`, a declared channel order, and the declared `FinishReason`. Anthropic serves it from run C or run A with `ToolCalls`. Put litellm, bedrock and openai/responses in UNCAPTURED for it. Put gemini and openai/chat in DECLINED with a wire reason. Serving the same bytes twice costs almost nothing.

### MAJOR

- **The `CleanStop` adjacency floor finds no real defect** - All six subjects pass it on the current fixtures. Bedrock, openai/chat, litellm and openai/responses give `[.., Usage, Finish]`. Anthropic gives `[Usage, Token, Token, Usage, Finish]`. Gemini gives `Token, Usage` for each chunk, then `Finish`. But the floor cannot see the Bedrock swap (§3.2). It also cannot see the SMA-522 fixture mistake. openai/chat and litellm buffer `Finish` until EOF, so a script with the usage chunk before the `finish_reason` chunk gives the same events. The contract lets `Usage` appear anywhere. On a tool stop, the chat and litellm `finish()` methods flush a buffered name after `Usage` and before `Finish` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:519-529, /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/stream.rs:739-754). The same rule on another scenario would fail conformant code. | Why it matters: the floor adds a rule that is not in the contract, and no bug class justifies it. §7 names gemini and anthropic as likely failures, but both pass. | Suggested fix: replace it with a positive-evidence floor: "`CleanStop` yields at least one `Usage`". Every `CleanStop` script carries usage. If Sven wants to keep the adjacency rule, its doc comment must say that it catches neither swap and applies only to `CleanStop`.

- **No floor proves that the `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` fixture has zero arguments** - The scenario gets only the generic tool floors. If the fixture changes to `{"city":"Berlin"}`, every check still passes. The scenario also has the `fixture_tool_name` conflict: `get_current_time` against `get_weather` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/lib.rs:199 and 560-567). | Why it matters: this is the vacuous pass that the SMA-533 §7.1 floors exist to prevent. | Suggested fix: use `fixture_calls` for both new scenarios. The zero-arg subject declares one call: name `get_current_time`, args `{}`. This also gives one solution to the name conflict for both scenarios.

- **UNCAPTURED gives a new way to hide a red scenario** - Each new scenario is served by exactly one subject. If that subject changes to `Uncaptured` and adds a row, the scenario runs for no subject, and nothing fails. Also, nothing prevents a subject from moving one of the nine SMA-533 scenarios into UNCAPTURED to hide a failing assertion. "Can occur, no capture" is true for almost any shape, so the bar is lower than for DECLINED. | Why it matters: SMA-533 §9.1 pinned DECLINED to close exactly this route. | Suggested fix: add two static unit tests in `declines.rs`. Test 1: for each entry in `Scenario::ALL`, at least one name in `REGISTERED_SUBJECTS` is in neither table. Test 2: UNCAPTURED rows can name only the scenarios that this change adds, from an explicit allow-list, so moving an older scenario needs a reviewed edit to that list.

### MINOR

- **Assertion 10 is stricter than the accumulator, but §3.4 says that it uses the same rule** - `build_items` parses into any `serde_json::Value` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:643-653). So `[1]` and `null` pass the accumulator. Gemini sets a missing `args` to `Value::Null` and sends `"null"` as `args_delta` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/sse.rs:45-52, stream.rs:57). | Why it matters: the `[1]` fake proves a rule that the consumer does not enforce. A Gemini zero-arg call can fail assertion 10 when its capture arrives. | Suggested fix: state that the rule is stricter on purpose, and give the reason. Record the Gemini `null` risk in the zero-arg follow-up issue. Note: every existing served tool fixture gives a JSON object, so assertion 10 passes on all of them today.

- **Assertion 10 runs on every scenario, including truncated, errored and cancelled ones** - A stream cut during the arguments correctly leaves partial JSON. No current fixture has this shape, so nothing fails yet. | Suggested fix: run assertion 10 only when the stream contains a `Finish`, because a consumer calls `finish()` only then. Also, instead of skipping every blank-id group, check the group when it carries exactly one name.

- **G2 is a fidelity rule, not a contract rule** - The contract says that `TokenDelta`, `ReasoningDelta` and `ToolCallDelta` "may interleave freely" (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:56-57). The accumulator also does not keep the order across channels. | Suggested fix: state in the floor's doc comment that it checks fidelity to the wire order, as the spec already does for the adjacency rule. Add a contract sentence only if Sven wants one.

- **`fixture_calls -> &'static [ExpectedCall]` with a `serde_json::Value` field cannot be a `const`** - An object `Value` needs an allocation, so each subject needs a `LazyLock` static. | Suggested fix: return `Vec<ExpectedCall>`, or store `args` as `&'static str` and parse it in the floor.

- **The per-call floor runs before `classify`** - In `ParallelToolCallCleanStop`, arguments that do not parse are reported as `ToolCallsMismatch` instead of the more exact `ToolArgsNotJsonObject`. The `floor_violation` doc says that floors leave the exact diagnosis to `classify` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/lib.rs:507-523). | Suggested fix: in the floor, skip a call whose arguments do not parse, and let assertion 10 report it.

- **The Bedrock order test is proven only by a manual mutation** - SMA-533 §8 says that a check by hand leaves nothing behind. The test also covers only `CleanStop`, but `ToolCallCleanStop` has the same two frames. | Suggested fix: put the check in a function that takes the chunk list. Unit-test that function on a swapped list. Run it on every script that has both frames.

- **Pitfalls in the Gemini parallel transcription** - The capture writes `"finishReason": "STOP"` with a space (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/tests/fixtures/parallel_signed.sse:7). The marker is `"finishReason":"` with no space (conformance.rs:2485). A byte-faithful copy therefore makes `encodes_stop_reason` return false. `tool_call_chunk` always adds `thoughtSignature` (conformance.rs:2575-2596), but only call 1 in the capture has one. `request()` must offer `search` and `weather`. The fixture file has no provenance header. | Suggested fix: name these three points in §6.9. Cite SMA-827 "Capture 1" in the transcription comment.

- **Some doc comments become false, but §6.10 says that the module docs are not edited** - These become false: the `floor_violation` doc (lib.rs:507-523), the `fixture_finish_reason` doc "Exactly four scenarios end with a Finish" (lib.rs:204), the `assert_conforms` doc (it names only DECLINED), rule 1 in the `conformance.rs` header (it names only `declines.rs`), and the anthropic module doc "this suite has no reasoning-delta scenario" (conformance.rs:1662-1666). | Suggested fix: list these sites in §6.10 as required edits.

- **Some negative tests are missing** - §6.8 covers the three content floors. It does not cover the new `InsufficientEvidence` floors: no `ReasoningDelta`, fewer than two `call_id`s, and a `None` channel order. It also does not name the UNCAPTURED versions of the three decline tests: unpinned, stale and drifted reason. `conforming()` for the parallel scenario needs two different `call_id`s, but `fakes::tool` uses the one constant `CALL_ID`. | Suggested fix: add these items to §6.8.

- **§6.7 "DECLINED, new rows" contains no rows** - The section lists two rows, then says that they belong in UNCAPTURED. | Suggested fix: write "No new DECLINED rows". After the D4 rework, add the gemini and openai/chat reasoning rows.

- **The scope of G6 and of the `Outcome::Uncaptured` doc is too wide** - Read literally, "no captured traffic for it is committed" also covers the seven Bedrock scenarios that are served from derived fixtures. | Suggested fix: write "each pair for a scenario that this change adds" and "no fixture that meets the provenance rule".

## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK
Most of the mechanics are sound: assertions 9 and 10, the two new scenarios, and the UNCAPTURED table. But three central claims are false when checked against the code: the G1 contract sentence conflicts with Bedrock, the anthropic thinking script has no text block, and the four UNCAPTURED thinking rows cannot be closed by a capture. §5 (D4, D5), §6.6 and §6.7 need rework, and one item needs a decision from Sven before implementation.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **The G1 contract sentence makes Bedrock non-conformant** - §3.3 checks only LiteLLM. The Bedrock SMA-833 path pushes an `Err`, then emits `Usage` when `metadata` arrives (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:150-160). The test `forbid_tool_calls_turns_a_tool_use_into_an_error` (same file, :848-869) asserts that `out[1]` is a `Usage` after the `Err`. The Bedrock driver yields every item from `consume` and does not return after an inner `Err` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/model.rs:173-177). The Anthropic driver also continues after an inner `Err`, for example a `refusal` at `message_stop` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/model.rs:150-154, stream.rs:383). The gemini, openai and litellm drivers return after an `Err`. No conformance scenario serves these paths, so assertion 9 stays green. | Why it matters: the PR would add a MUST to core that a published crate breaks, and a test in that crate pins the breach. §7 says that a defect that needs a design decision stops the work. | Suggested fix: decide before implementation. Option A: the Bedrock and Anthropic drivers return after they yield an inner `Err`, and the Bedrock test changes, so the `Usage` after the error is lost. Option B: the sentence allows `Usage` after `Err`, and assertion 9 exempts it. In both cases, add a translator-level test, because the suite cannot reach this path.

- **The anthropic thinking script has no text block, so the declared order `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]` fails** - The served `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop` script removes the text block of the capture (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs:2092-2119; the comment at 2097-2100 says so). With the current translator, the observed runs are `[Reasoning, Tool]`. So the D4 statement "the suite already serves exactly that capture" is false. §6.8 gives the conforming fake `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]`, so the unit tests stay green and do not show the mismatch. | Why it matters: as written, anthropic fails with `ChannelOrderMismatch` on the first run. Or the builder changes the declaration to `[Reasoning, Tool]`, which cannot show that text stays between reasoning and the tool call. That is the main property that G2 can test. | Suggested fix: tell the builder to restore the text block from `thinking_text_tool_use.txt` (text at index 1, `tool_use` at index 2), to update the provenance comment, and to declare `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]`. The text block then emits a Text-position `ProviderData` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:275-279). Assertion 8 still passes, because that event has no `call_id`. A better fix: measure the channel order from the script bytes, as `encodes_stop_reason` does, so that this drift fails automatically.

- **The four UNCAPTURED rows for `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop` are false, and D5 contradicts itself** - The scenario floor requires a call-scoped `ProviderData` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/lib.rs:574-588). After this change, it also requires at least one `ReasoningDelta`. Only the anthropic and gemini streams emit `ProviderData`. The bedrock, litellm and openai/responses stream translators emit none. Gemini emits no `ReasoningDelta` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/lib.rs:59-60). Its request never sets `includeThoughts` or `thinkingConfig`, so no thought part comes on the wire. A capture alone cannot let any of the four subjects serve this scenario. Also, the new openai/chat reason "the chat translator reads no reasoning field" is about the translator, which D5 itself forbids. The same reason applies to gemini, but gemini goes to UNCAPTURED. | Why it matters: the pinned table would say "only a capture is missing" when that is not true, and the follow-up issue cannot be closed as written. The anti-goals forbid this kind of false table row. | Suggested fix: reverse D4. Keep `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop` as the anthropic signed-thinking scenario. Rewrite its DECLINED reasons as true statements, for example "the stream emits no call-scoped ProviderData for a thinking block". Add a provider-neutral `ReasoningCleanStop` with three floors: at least one `ReasoningDelta`, a declared channel order, and the declared `FinishReason`. Anthropic serves it from run C or run A with `ToolCalls`. Put litellm, bedrock and openai/responses in UNCAPTURED for it. Put gemini and openai/chat in DECLINED with a wire reason. Serving the same bytes twice costs almost nothing.

### MAJOR

- **The `CleanStop` adjacency floor finds no real defect** - All six subjects pass it on the current fixtures. Bedrock, openai/chat, litellm and openai/responses give `[.., Usage, Finish]`. Anthropic gives `[Usage, Token, Token, Usage, Finish]`. Gemini gives `Token, Usage` for each chunk, then `Finish`. But the floor cannot see the Bedrock swap (§3.2). It also cannot see the SMA-522 fixture mistake. openai/chat and litellm buffer `Finish` until EOF, so a script with the usage chunk before the `finish_reason` chunk gives the same events. The contract lets `Usage` appear anywhere. On a tool stop, the chat and litellm `finish()` methods flush a buffered name after `Usage` and before `Finish` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:519-529, /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/stream.rs:739-754). The same rule on another scenario would fail conformant code. | Why it matters: the floor adds a rule that is not in the contract, and no bug class justifies it. §7 names gemini and anthropic as likely failures, but both pass. | Suggested fix: replace it with a positive-evidence floor: "`CleanStop` yields at least one `Usage`". Every `CleanStop` script carries usage. If Sven wants to keep the adjacency rule, its doc comment must say that it catches neither swap and applies only to `CleanStop`.

- **No floor proves that the `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` fixture has zero arguments** - The scenario gets only the generic tool floors. If the fixture changes to `{"city":"Berlin"}`, every check still passes. The scenario also has the `fixture_tool_name` conflict: `get_current_time` against `get_weather` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/lib.rs:199 and 560-567). | Why it matters: this is the vacuous pass that the SMA-533 §7.1 floors exist to prevent. | Suggested fix: use `fixture_calls` for both new scenarios. The zero-arg subject declares one call: name `get_current_time`, args `{}`. This also gives one solution to the name conflict for both scenarios.

- **UNCAPTURED gives a new way to hide a red scenario** - Each new scenario is served by exactly one subject. If that subject changes to `Uncaptured` and adds a row, the scenario runs for no subject, and nothing fails. Also, nothing prevents a subject from moving one of the nine SMA-533 scenarios into UNCAPTURED to hide a failing assertion. "Can occur, no capture" is true for almost any shape, so the bar is lower than for DECLINED. | Why it matters: SMA-533 §9.1 pinned DECLINED to close exactly this route. | Suggested fix: add two static unit tests in `declines.rs`. Test 1: for each entry in `Scenario::ALL`, at least one name in `REGISTERED_SUBJECTS` is in neither table. Test 2: UNCAPTURED rows can name only the scenarios that this change adds, from an explicit allow-list, so moving an older scenario needs a reviewed edit to that list.

### MINOR

- **Assertion 10 is stricter than the accumulator, but §3.4 says that it uses the same rule** - `build_items` parses into any `serde_json::Value` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:643-653). So `[1]` and `null` pass the accumulator. Gemini sets a missing `args` to `Value::Null` and sends `"null"` as `args_delta` (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/sse.rs:45-52, stream.rs:57). | Why it matters: the `[1]` fake proves a rule that the consumer does not enforce. A Gemini zero-arg call can fail assertion 10 when its capture arrives. | Suggested fix: state that the rule is stricter on purpose, and give the reason. Record the Gemini `null` risk in the zero-arg follow-up issue. Note: every existing served tool fixture gives a JSON object, so assertion 10 passes on all of them today.

- **Assertion 10 runs on every scenario, including truncated, errored and cancelled ones** - A stream cut during the arguments correctly leaves partial JSON. No current fixture has this shape, so nothing fails yet. | Suggested fix: run assertion 10 only when the stream contains a `Finish`, because a consumer calls `finish()` only then. Also, instead of skipping every blank-id group, check the group when it carries exactly one name.

- **G2 is a fidelity rule, not a contract rule** - The contract says that `TokenDelta`, `ReasoningDelta` and `ToolCallDelta` "may interleave freely" (/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:56-57). The accumulator also does not keep the order across channels. | Suggested fix: state in the floor's doc comment that it checks fidelity to the wire order, as the spec already does for the adjacency rule. Add a contract sentence only if Sven wants one.

- **`fixture_calls -> &'static [ExpectedCall]` with a `serde_json::Value` field cannot be a `const`** - An object `Value` needs an allocation, so each subject needs a `LazyLock` static. | Suggested fix: return `Vec<ExpectedCall>`, or store `args` as `&'static str` and parse it in the floor.

The test also covers only `CleanStop`, but `ToolCallCleanStop` has the same two frames. | Suggested fix: put the check in a function that takes the chunk list.
